Routines.Name: Blackbody
Routines.DisplayName: Blackbody band emission
Routines.ShortDescription: Blackbody determines the emission for a blackbody in a certain wavelength interval
Routines.LongDescription: Blackbody is an EES function that returns the band emission ratio for a blackbody in a certain wavelength interval.  The band emission is the ratio of the black body emissive power between the two provided wavelengths to the total blackbody emissive power.

Routines.Name: Eb
Routines.DisplayName: Blackbody spectral emissive power
Routines.ShortDescription: Eb implements Planck's Law to provid the spectral emissive power of a blackbody.
Routines.LongDescription: Eb is an EES function that returns the spectral emissive power of a blackbody given its temperature (in K only) and the wavelength (in micron only).

Routines.Name: Nucleate_Boiling_Rohsenow
Routines.DisplayName: Nucleate Boiling (Rohsenow correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Nucleate_Boiling_Rohsenow returns the surface heat flux in nucleate boiling calculated using the Rohsenow correlation.
Routines.LongDescription: The function Nucleate_Boiling_Rohsenow returns the surface heat flux for nucleate boiling of a fluid by means of a heated surface of a specified material.  This procedure is responsible for determining the property data of the specified fluid. It uses the correlation developed by Rohsenow (1952). This function should be used only as a rough estimate of the heat flux as errors of 100% are common.

Routines.Name: Nucleate_Boiling_Kutateladze
Routines.DisplayName: Nucleate Boiling (Kutateladze correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Nucleate_Boiling_Kutateladze returns the surface heat flux in nucleate boiling calculated using the Kutateladze correlation.
Routines.LongDescription:
The function Nucleate_Boiling_Kutateladze returns the surface heat flux for nucleate boiling of a fluid by means of a heated surface of a specified material.  
This procedure is responsible for determining the property data of the specified fluid. It uses the correlation developed by Kutateladze (1952). (Kutateladze, S. S., 1952.  Heat Transfer in Condensation and Boiling, 2nd ed.  Moscow: State Science and Technology Publications of Literature on Machinery).

Routines.Name: Nucleate_Boiling_Cooper
Routines.DisplayName: Nucleate Boiling (Cooper correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Nucleate_Boiling_Cooper returns the surface heat flux in nucleate boiling calculated using the Cooper correlation.
Routines.LongDescription: The function Nucleate_Boiling_Cooper returns the surface heat flux for nucleate boiling of a fluid.  This correlation is presented in Chapter 11 of Ghiaasiaan (2008) and is based on the work of Cooper (1984).  This procedure is responsible for determining the property data of the specified fluid and implementing the correlation.

Routines.Name: Nucleate_Boiling_Gorenflo
Routines.DisplayName: Nucleate Boiling (Gorenflo correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Nucleate_Boiling_Gorenflo returns the surface heat flux in nucleate boiling calculated using the Gorenflo correlation.
Routines.LongDescription: The function Nucleate_Boiling_Gorenflo returns the surface heat flux for nucleate boiling of a fluid.  This correlation is presented in Chapter 11 of Ghiaasiaan (2008) and is based on the work of Leiner and Gorenflo (1992).

Routines.Name: Critical_Heat_Flux_Lienhard
Routines.DisplayName: Critical Heat Flux (Lienhard correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Critical_Heat_Flux_Lienhard returns the critical heat flux using the Lienhard correlation.
Routines.LongDescription: Critical_Heat_Flux_Lienhard returns the critical heat flux in for the specified fluid and geometry using the correlation provided in Eq. 7-4 of Nellis and Klein (2009) which is based on the work of Lienhard and Dhir (1973).

Routines.Name: Critical_Heat_Flux_Gh
Routines.DisplayName: Critical Heat Flux (Ghiaasiaan correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Critical_Heat_Flux_Gh returns the critical heat flux using the Ghiaasiaan correlation.
Routines.LongDescription:
Critical_Heat_Flux_Gh returns the critical heat flux in for the specified fluid and geometry using the information provided in Ghiaasiaan (2008).  The correlation suggested by Sun and Lienhard (1970) is used to compute the critical heat flux and then corrections are applied for:
1. geometry based on work from Sun and Lienhard (1970), Ded and Lienhard (1972), and Lienhard and Dhir (1970)
2. contact angle based on Haramura (1999)
3. angle relative to horizontal based on Chang and You (1996)
4. liquid subcooling based on Elkassabgi and Lienhard (1988)

Routines.Name: Film_Boiling_Bromley
Routines.DisplayName: Film Boiling (Bromley correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Film_Boiling_Bromley returns the surface heat flux for film boiling using the Bromley correlation.
Routines.LongDescription: The function Film_Boiling_Bromley returns the surface heat flux for film boiling of a fluid by means of a heated horizontal cylindrical or spherical surface.  It uses the correlation developed by Bromley (1950) as reported in Incropera and DeWitt (2002).  The heat transfer coefficient associated with the surface heat flux that is calculated includes contributions from convection and radiation.

Routines.Name: Film_Boiling_Berenson
Routines.DisplayName: Film Boiling (Berenson correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Film_Boiling_Berenson returns the surface heat flux for film boiling of a fluid from a heated horizontal tube with the Berenson correlation.
Routines.LongDescription: The function Film_Boiling_Berenson returns the surface heat flux for film boiling of a fluid by means of a heated horizontal tube.  It uses the correlation developed by Berenson (1961).  The heat transfer coefficient associated with the surface heat flux that is calculated includes contributions from convection and radiation.

Routines.Name: Film_Boiling_Breen
Routines.DisplayName: Film Boiling (Breen correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Film_Boiling_Breen returns the surface heat flux for film boiling of a fluid from a heated horizontal flat surface with the Breen correlation.
Routines.LongDescription: The function Film_Boiling_Breen returns the surface heat flux for film boiling of a fluid by means of a heated horizontal flat surface.  It uses the correlation developed by Breen and Westwater (1962).  The heat transfer coefficient associated with the surface heat flux that is calculated includes contributions from convection and radiation.

Routines.Name: T_MFB_Zuber
Routines.DisplayName: Minimum Film Boiling Temperature (Zuber correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: T_MFB_Zuber returns the minimum film boiling temperature using the Zuber correlation.
Routines.LongDescription: T_MFB_Zuber returns the minimum film boiling temperature.   It uses the correlation developed by Zuber (1959).

Routines.Name: Flow_Boiling_Shah
Routines.DisplayName: Local flow boiling heat transfer coefficient (Shah correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Flow_Boiling_Shah implements the Shah (1982) correlation to determine the local heat transfer coefficient for a boiling fluid in a tube.
Routines.LongDescription: The procedure Flow_Boiling_Shah implements the Shah (1982) correlation to determine the local heat transfer coefficient for a boiling fluid in a tube considering both convective and nucleate boiling contributions as discussed in section 7.3.2 of Heat Transfer by Nellis and Klein (2009) using the correlation developed by Shah (1982).   At x=1, the procedure returns that heat transfer coefficient expected for a single phase vapor at the given mass velocity and diameter.  At high values of quality that would result in a Reynold's number less than 2300, linear interpolation is used between the heat transfer coefficient at a quality that results in Re=2300 and the x=1 value.

Routines.Name: Flow_Boiling_Chen
Routines.DisplayName: Local flow boiling heat transfer coefficient (Chen correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Flow_Boiling_Chen implements the Chen (1966) correlation to determine the local heat transfer coefficient for a boiling fluid in a vertical tube.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Flow_Boiling_Chen implements the Chen (1966) correlation{linkID=90009} for boiling heat transfer with saturated fluids in convective flow to determine the heat transfer coefficient for a boiling fluid in a vertical tube considering both convective and nucleate boiling contributions.

Routines.Name: Flow_Boiling_Hamilton
Routines.DisplayName: Local flow boiling heat transfer coefficient (Hamilton correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Flow_Boiling_Hamilton implements the Hamilton (2008) correlation to determine the local heat transfer coefficient for a boiling fluid in a microtube
Routines.LongDescription: Flow_Boiling_Hamilton implements the Hamilton (2008) correlation to determine the heat transfer coefficient for an evaporating refrigerant in a micro-tube heat exchanger.  The correlation is applicable to pure refrigerants and blends.  The correction for blends uses the approximation reported in Kedzierski et al. (2015).  At x=1, the procedure returns that heat transfer coefficient expected for a single phase vapor at the given mass velocity and diameter.  At high values of quality that would result in a Reynold's number less than 2300, linear interpolation is used between the heat transfer coefficient at a quality that results in Re=2300 and the x=1 value.

Routines.Name: Flow_Boiling_Shah_avg
Routines.DisplayName: Average flow boiling heat transfer coefficient (Shen correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Flow_Boiling_Shah_avg calculates the average heat transfer coefficient for boiling of a two-phase fluid inside a circular tube.
Routines.LongDescription: Flow_Boiling_Shah_avg calculates the average heat transfer coefficient for boiling of a two-phase fluid inside a circular tube entering with of vapor at quality x_in and exiting with quality x_out.  This procedure uses the Flow_Boiling_Shah  procedure to determine the local heat transfer coefficient and wall temperature at discrete values of quality. It then integrates these values over the range of quality and returns the integrated average heat transfer coefficient.

Routines.Name: Flow_Boiling_Hamilton_avg
Routines.DisplayName: Average flow boiling heat transfer coefficient (Hamilton correlation)
Routines.ShortDescription: Flow_Boiling_Hamilton_avg calculates the average heat transfer coefficient for boiling of a two-phase fluid inside a circular tube.
Routines.LongDescription: Flow_Boiling_Hamilton_avg calculates the average convective boiling heat transfer coefficient by repeated calls to the Flow_Boiling_Hamilton procedure over the specified quality range to determine the local heat transfer coefficient.  This correlation is applicable for saturated boiling of pure fluids.

Routines.Name: CHF_local
Routines.DisplayName: Local critical heat flux in flow boiling
Routines.ShortDescription: CHF_Local returns the critical heat flux for flow boiling of water flowing through a vertical tube.
Routines.LongDescription: CHF_Local returns the critical heat flux for flow boiling of water flowing through a vertical tube.  The function interpolates from the database presented by Groeneveld et al. (2007) which provides tables of CHF for 8 mm diameter tubes in the parameter space of mass flux, quality, and pressure.  The result is corrected for diameter using the method suggested by Groeneveld (2007).

Routines.Name: CHF_tube
Routines.DisplayName: Critical heat flux for flow boiling in a length of tube
Routines.ShortDescription: CHF_Tube returns the critical heat flux for flow boiling of water flowing through a length of vertical tube as well as the inlet temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: CHF_Tube returns the critical heat flux for flow boiling of water flowing through a vertical tube as well as the inlet temperature.  The function uses the technique presented by Groeneveld et al. (2007) to determine the maximum uniform heat flux that can be applied to a vertical tube with water flowing through it before the critical heat flux phenomenon is experienced at the outlet.

Routines.Name: Cond_Tube
Routines.DisplayName: Local condensation heat transfer coefficient in a tube.
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_Tube calculates the local heat transfer coefficient for condensation of saturated vapor in plain conventional channels and mini/micro channels for all orientations.
Routines.LongDescription: Cond_Tube calculates the local heat transfer coefficient for condensation of saturated vapor of quality, x, in plain conventional channels and mini/micro channels for all orientations.  This procedure implements the correlations presented in Shah (2016).

Routines.Name: Cond_Tube_Avg
Routines.DisplayName: Average condensation heat transfer coefficient in a tube.
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_Tube_Avg calculates the average heat transfer coefficient for condensation of a two-phase fluid inside a tube.
Routines.LongDescription: Cond_Tube_avg calculates the average heat transfer coefficient for condensation of vapor inside a circular tube using the correlations from Shah (2016).  This procedure uses the Cond_Tube procedure to supply values for the mean heat transfer coefficient at discrete values of quality. It then integrates these values and returns the average heat transfer coefficient.

Routines.Name: Cond_HorizontalTube
Routines.DisplayName: Local condensation heat transfer coefficient in a horizontal tube.
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_HorizontalTube calculates the local heat transfer coefficient for condensation of a two-phase fluid inside a horizontal tube.
Routines.LongDescription:
Cond_HorizontalTube calculates the heat transfer coefficient for condensation of saturated vapor inside a circular tube.   The latent heat of evaporation is modified based on the correction term developed by Rohsenow (1956) that accounts for the nonlinearity of the temperature profile due to convection effects.  The correlation used is that of Dobson and Chato (1998) as presented in section 7.5.2 of Nellis and Klein.  
If m_dot (the mass flowrate) is set to 0, the procedure returns the heat transfer coefficient corresponding to film condensation recommended by Chato (1962).

Routines.Name: Cond_HorizontalTube_avg
Routines.DisplayName: Average condensation heat transfer coefficient in a horizontal tube.
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_HorizontalTube_avg calculates the average heat transfer coefficient for condensation of a two-phase fluid inside a horizontal tube.
Routines.LongDescription: Cond_HorizontalTube_avg calculates the average heat transfer coefficient for condensation of vapor.  This procedure uses the Cond_HorizontalTube procedure to supply values for the mean heat transfer coefficient using the Dobson and Chato correlation at discrete values of quality. It then integrates these values and returns the average heat transfer coefficient.

Routines.Name: Cond_Vertical_Plate
Routines.DisplayName: Condensation heat transfer from a vertical plate
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_vertical_plate calculates the heat transfer coefficient for condensation on a flat vertical plate in quiescent saturated vapor.
Routines.LongDescription: Cond_vertical_plate calculates the heat transfer coefficient for condensation on a flat vertical plate in quiescent saturated vapor.  The latent heat of evaporation is modified based on the correction term developed by Rohsenow (1956). This correction term accounts for the nonlinearity of the temperature profile due to convection effects. Three different correlations applying to three different ranges of Reynolds numbers are combined.  The correlations are recommended by Butterworth (1981) and partially based off of results determined by Labuntsov (1957) as presented in section 7.4.3 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: Cond_Horizontal_Cylinder
Routines.DisplayName: Condensation heat transfer from a horizontal cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_horizontal_Cylinder calculates the heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number for condensation on a horizontal cylinder in quiescent saturated vapor.
Routines.LongDescription: Cond_horizontal_Cylinder(Fluid$, T_sat, T_w, D:h_m, Nusselt_m) calculates the heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number for condensation on a horizontal cylinder in quiescent saturated vapor. This procedure is responsible for determining the property data of the specified fluid. The latent heat of evaporation is modified based on the correction term given in Rohsenow (1998). This correction term accounts for condensate subcooling. The function Cond_Horizontal_Cylinder uses the correlation provided in Rohsenow (1998) as presented in section 7.4.3 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: Cond_Horizontal_N_Cylinders
Routines.DisplayName: Condensation heat transfer from a bank of horizontal cylinders
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_horizontal_Cylinder calculates the heat transfer coefficient for condensation on a bank of horizontal cylinders arranged vertically in quiescent saturated vapor.
Routines.LongDescription: Cond_horizontal_Cylinder calculates the heat transfer coefficient for condensation on a bank of horizontal cylinders arranged vertically in quiescent saturated vapor.  The procedure discounts the heat transfer coefficient determined with the Cond_horizontal_cylinder function to account for condensate innundation, as described in section 7.4 of Kakac and Liu (1997) and presented in section 7.4.3 of Nellis and Klein (2009).

Routines.Name: Cond_Finned_Tube
Routines.DisplayName: Condensation heat transfer from a horizontal cylinder with annular fins
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_finned_tube calculates the heat transfer coefficient for condensation on a finned horizontal tube in quiescent saturated vapor.
Routines.LongDescription: Cond_finned_tube calculates the heat transfer coefficient for condensation on a finned horizontal tube in quiescent saturated vapor.  The latent heat of evaporation is modified based on the correction term developed by Rohsenow (1956) to account for the nonlinearity of the temperature profile due to convection effects. The Beatty and Katz (1948) correlation is used. Condensation along the edge of the fins is not considered.  Cond_finned_tube calls eta_fin_annular_rect to determine the fin efficiency which is then used to determine the heat transfer coefficient in an iterative process as described in section 7.4.3 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: Cond_Horizontal_Up
Routines.DisplayName: Condensation heat transfer from the upper surface of a cooled plate.
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_horizontal_up calculates the heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number for condensation on a horizontal flat plate with the cooled side facing upwards.
Routines.LongDescription: Cond_horizontal_up calculates the heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number for condensation on a horizontal flat plate with the cooled side facing upwards.  The latent heat of evaporation is modified based on the correction term developed by Rohsenow (1956) to account for the nonlinearity of the temperature profile due to convection effects. The correlation developed by Nimmo and Leppert (1970) as presented in section 7.4.3 of Nellis and Klein is used.  This correlation assumes that the plate is bounded on the edges parallel to the flow direction and neglects surface tension effects.

Routines.Name: Cond_Horizontal_Down
Routines.DisplayName: Condensation heat transfer from the bottom surface of a cooled plate.
Routines.ShortDescription: Cond_horizontal_down calculates the heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number for condensation on a horizontal flat plate with the cooled side facing downward.
Routines.LongDescription: Cond_horizontal_down calculates the heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number for condensation on a horizontal flat plate with the cooled side facing downward. The latent heat of evaporation is modified based on the correction term developed by Rohsenow (1956) to account for the nonlinearity of the temperature profile due to convection effects. The function uses the correlation developed by Gerstmann and Griffith (1967) as presented in Nellis and Klein. This correlation is based on the condensate being removed as droplets, which formed due to Taylor instability on the condensate surface.

Routines.Name: DELTAP_2phase_horiz
Routines.DisplayName: Two phase pressure drop in a horizontal tube
Routines.ShortDescription: DELTAP_2phase_horiz returns the two-phase pressure drop in a horizontal tube.
Routines.LongDescription: DELTAP_2phase_horiz returns the two-phase pressure drop in a horizontal tube. The pressure drop is the sum of the frictional pressure drop and the momentum pressure drop. The momentum pressure drop is calculated using a void fraction obtained from drift flux model, as described by Ould Didi et al. (2002).  The Muller-Steinhagen and Heck correlation described  by Ould Didi et al. (2002) is used to predict the pressure gradient.  The pressure gradient is then integrated to determine the pressure drop from inlet to outlet.  The heat flux is assumed to be constant along the length of the tube so that dL/dx is constant.

Routines.Name: SR_7
Routines.DisplayName: Resistance between hyperellipse contact with uniform heat flux and semi-infinite body
Routines.ShortDescription: SR_7 returns the thermal resistance between the surface of a hyperellipse contact area that is exposed to a uniform heat flux and is located on the surface of a semi-infinite half-space.  The resistance is based on the center temperature of the ellipse.
Routines.LongDescription: SR_7 returns the thermal resistance between the surface of a hyperellipse contact area that is exposed to a uniform heat flux and is located on the surface of a semi-infinite half-space.  The resistance is based on the center temperature of the ellipse.  A hyperellipse is defined by the equation:  (x/a)^n + (y/b)^n = 1 where a  is the major radius and b  is the minor radius (a >= b ).  When n = 2 the hyperellipse is just an ellipse and when a = b and n = 2 the hyperellipse becomes a circle.  Larger values of n result in a more rectangular shape with rounded edges.  The limits of the solution are: 0.1< a/b < 1 and n>0.5.

Routines.Name: SR_11
Routines.DisplayName: Resistance between circle with contact resistance and semi-infinite body
Routines.ShortDescription: SR_11 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area located on the surface of a semi-infinite half-space.  The resistance that is calculated is based only on the conduction resistance in the half-space (i.e., the resistance of the interface is not included).
Routines.LongDescription: SR_11 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area located on the surface of a semi-infinite half-space.  The resistance that is calculated is based only on the conduction resistance in the half-space (i.e., the resistance of the interface is not included).  The resistance is therefore based on the average temperature on the material-side of the contact.  The contact area itself is assumed to be at a uniform temperature.  Note that if the conductance approaches zero then the result limits to the uniform heat flux result (SR_2) while if the conductance approaches infinity then the result limits to the uniform temperature result (SR_1).  Note that the total resistance between the contact and the material far from the half space is R_total = 1/(h*pi*a^2) + SR_11  (the function SR_11 calculates only the spreading resistance).  The solution is from Rohsenow, W.M, J. P. Hartnett, and Y. I. Cho, Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill, (1998).

Routines.Name: SR_12
Routines.DisplayName: Resistance between square with contact resistance and semi-infinite body
Routines.ShortDescription: SR_12 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a square contact area located on the surface of a semi-infinite half-space.  The resistance that is calculated is based only on the conduction resistance in the half-space (i.e., the resistance of the interface is not included).
Routines.LongDescription: SR_12 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a square contact area located on the surface of a semi-infinite half-space.  The resistance that is calculated is based only on the conduction resistance in the half-space (i.e., the resistance of the interface is not included). The resistance is therefore based on the average temperature on the material-side of the contact.  The contact area itself is assumed to be at a uniform temperature.  Note that if the conductance approaches zero then the result limits to the uniform heat flux result (SR_5) while if the conductance approaches infinity then the result limits to the uniform temperature result.  Note that the total resistance between the contact and the material far from the half space is R_total = 1/(h*4*a^2) + SR_12  (function SR_12 calculates only the spreading resistance).   Solution is from Rohsenow, W.M, J. P. Hartnett, and Y. I. Cho, Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill, (1998).

Routines.Name: SR_13
Routines.DisplayName: Resistance between circle on a cylindrical flux tube
Routines.ShortDescription: SR_13 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area with constant heat flux located on the surface of an infinitely long circular flux tube.  The spreading resistance is the thermal resistance that is in addition to the 1-D thermal resistance in the flux tube that would exist if the heat flux was applied uniformly over the entire area of the tube.
Routines.LongDescription:
SR_13 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area with constant heat flux located on the surface of an infinitely long circular flux tube.  The spreading resistance is the thermal resistance that is in addition to the 1-D thermal resistance in the flux tube that would exist if the heat flux was applied uniformly over the entire area of the tube.  The resistance is based on the average temperature over the area.  The contact area itself is assumed to be exposed to a uniform heat flux.  Note that if a << b then the result approaches the equivalent result for spreading resistance from a half-space given by SR_2.  Note that the total resistance associated with conduction through a circular bar of length L with a contact on one end will be the sum of the normal, 1D resistance and the spreading resistance: 
R_total = L/(k*pi*b^2) + SR_13 (SR_13 only calculates the additional resistance associated with spreading that occurs at the end of the bar).   Solution is from Rohsenow, W.M, J. P. Hartnett, and Y. I. Cho, Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill, (1998).

Routines.Name: SR_14
Routines.DisplayName: Resistance between circle on a cylindrical flux tube
Routines.ShortDescription: SR_14 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area located on the surface of an infinitely long circular flux tube.  The contact area itself is assumed to be exposed to a uniform temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: SR_14 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area located on the surface of an infinitely long circular flux tube.  The contact area itself is assumed to be exposed to a uniform temperature.  The spreading resistance is the thermal resistance that is in addition to the 1-D thermal resistance in the flux tube that would exist if the uniform temperature existed over the entire area of the tube.  Note that if a << b then the result approaches the equivalent result for spreading resistance from a half-space given by SR_1.  Note that the total resistance associated with conduction through a circular bar of length L with a contact on one end will be the sum of the normal, 1D resistance and the spreading resistance:  R_total = L/(k*pi*b^2) + SR_14 (SR_14 only calculates the additional resistance associated with spreading that occurs at the end of the bar).  The solution is from Rohsenow, W.M, J. P. Hartnett, and Y. I. Cho, Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill, (1998).

Routines.Name: SR_15
Routines.DisplayName: Resistance between circle on a square flux tube
Routines.ShortDescription: SR_15 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area located on the surface of an infinitely long square flux tube.  The contact area itself is assumed to be exposed to a uniform heat flux.
Routines.LongDescription:
SR_15 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area located on the surface of an infinitely long square flux tube.  The contact area itself is assumed to be exposed to a uniform heat flux.  The spreading resistance is the thermal resistance that is in addition to the 1-D thermal resistance in the flux tube that would exist if the uniform heat flux was applied over the entire area of the tube.  

Note that if a << b then the result approaches the equivalent result for spreading resistance from a half-space given by SR_2.  Note that the total resistance associated with conduction through a circular bar of length L with a contact on one end will be the sum of the normal, 1D resistance and the spreading resistance: R_total = L/(k*4*b^2) + SR_15 (SR_15 only calculates the additional resistance associated with spreading that occurs at the end of the bar).  The solution is from Rohsenow, W.M, J. P. Hartnett, and Y. I. Cho, Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3rd Edition, McGraw Hill, (1998).

Routines.Name: SR_16
Routines.DisplayName: Resistance between circle on a square flux tube
Routines.ShortDescription: SR_16 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area located on the surface of an infinitely long square flux tube.  The contact area itself is assumed to be exposed to a uniform temperature.
Routines.LongDescription:
SR_16 returns the thermal resistance associated with spreading between a circular contact area located on the surface of an infinitely long square flux tube.  The contact area itself is assumed to be exposed to a uniform temperature.  The spreading resistance is the thermal resistance that is in addition to the 1-D thermal resistance in the flux tube that would exist if the uniform temperature was applied over the entire area of the tube.  

Note that if a << b then the result approaches the equivalent result for spreading resistance from a half-space given by SR_1.  Note that the total resistance associated with conduction through a circular bar of length L with a contact on one end will be the sum of the normal, 1D resistance and the spreading resistance: R_total = L/(k*4*b^2) + SR_16 (SR_16 only calculates the additional resistance associated with spreading that occurs at the end of the bar). Routines.Name: PipeFlow
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a round pipe
Routines.ShortDescription: PipeFlow returns lower and upper bounds on the average heat transfer coefficient and the pressure drop for a specified mass flow rate through a circular tube.
Routines.LongDescription: PipeFlow returns lower and upper bounds on the average heat transfer coefficient and the pressure drop for a specified mass flow rate through a circular tube.  The procedure assumes simultaneous hydrodynamic and thermally developing flow as reported in Section 5.2.3 of Nellis and Klein. Two values of the heat transfer coefficient are returned.  The first, h_T is determined assuming that the wall is at constant temperature.  The second is determined assuming that the wall is subjected to a constant heat flux.  For laminar flow, these values should provide lower and upper bounds on the heat transfer coefficient.  For turbulent flow, these values are identical.  The procedure will determine if the flow is laminar or turbulent.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynold's numbers between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations.  The ratio of L/D is used to apply a developing flow correction based on simultaneous hydrodynamic and thermal development; set L to a large number if developing flow corrections are not applicable.  Note that a negative value of mass flow rate leads to a negative pressure drop.

The procedure assumes simultaneous hydrodynamic and thermally developing flow as reported in Section 5.2.3 of Nellis and Klein. Two values of the heat transfer coefficient are returned. For laminar flow, these values should provide lower and upper bounds on the heat transfer coefficient.  For turbulent flow, these values are identical.  The procedure will determine if the flow is laminar or turbulent.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynold's numbers between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations.  The ratio of L/D is used to apply a developing flow correction based on simultaneous hydrodynamic and thermal development; set L to a large number if developing flow corrections are not applicable.  Note that a negative value of mass flow rate leads to a negative pressure drop.

Routines.Name: AnnularFlow
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through an annular duct - heat transfer to inner surface
Routines.ShortDescription: AnnularFlow returns lower and upper bounds on the average heat transfer coefficient and the pressure drop for a specified mass flow rate through an annuar duct.
Routines.LongDescription: AnnularFlow returns the lower and upper bounds on the convection coefficient for developing or fully-developed flow in an annular duct.  The outer wall of the annulus is assumed to be insulated so heat transfer occurs across the wall separating the annulus from the pipe.  The area used for heat transfer should be the area of this wall.  Two values of the heat transfer coefficient are returned that should provide upper and lower bounds.  These heat transfer coefficients are both for the inner annular wall with an insulated outer wall.  For turbulent flow, these values are identical.  The procedure will determine if the flow is laminar or turbulent.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynold's numbers between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations. Note that a negative value of mass flow rate leads to a negative pressure drop.

Routines.Name: AnnularFlow_outer
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through an annular duct - heat transfer to outer surface
Routines.ShortDescription: AnnularFlow_Outer returns the lower and upper bounds on the convection coefficient for developing or fully-developed flow in an annular duct with the outer tube heated.
Routines.LongDescription: AnnularFlow_Outer returns the lower and upper bounds on the convection coefficient for developing or fully-developed flow in an annular duct with the outer tube heated.   The inner wall of the annulus is assumed to be insulated so heat transfer occurs across the outer wall.  The area used for heat transfer should be the area of the outer tubel.  The procedure also returns the friction factor for these conditions.  Two values of the heat transfer coefficient are returned that should provide upper and lower bounds.  These heat transfer coefficients are both for the outer annular wall with an insulated inner wall.  For turbulent flow, these values are identical.  The procedure will determine if the flow is laminar or turbulent.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynold's numbers between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations. Note that a negative values of mass flow rate leads to a negative pressure drop.

Routines.Name: HelicalPipeFlow
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a pipe that is wrapped in a helix.
Routines.ShortDescription: HelicalPipeFlow returns lower and upper bounds on the average heat transfer coefficient and the pressure drop for a specified mass flow rate through a circular tube that is wound in a helix.
Routines.LongDescription: HelicalPipeFlow returns lower and upper bounds on the average heat transfer coefficient and the pressure drop for a specified mass flow rate through a circular tube that is wound in a helix. The procedure modifies the results for a straight tube (obtained using the procedure PipeFlow) as discussed in the Heat Exchanger Design Handbook and Barron.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynold's numbers between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations. The ratio of L/D is used to apply a developing flow correction based on simultaneous hydrodynamic and thermal development; set L to a large number if developing flow corrections are not applicable.  Two values of the heat transfer coefficient are returned. The first, h_T is determined assuming that the wall is at constant temperature. The second is determined assuming that the wall is subjected to a constant heat flux. For laminar flow, these values should provide lower and upper bounds on the heat transfer coefficient. For turbulent flow, these values are identical. Note that a negative value of mass flow rate leads to a negative pressure drop.

Routines.Name: Tube_Bundle
Routines.DisplayName: Flow along a tube bundle
Routines.ShortDescription: Tube_Bundle returns the average heat transfer coefficient and the pressure drop for flow through an ideal tube bundle having either square or triangular tube layout.
Routines.LongDescription: Tube_Bundle returns the average heat transfer coefficient and the pressure drop for flow through an ideal tube bundle having either square or triangular tube layout.  Flow can be vertical (up or down) or horizontal.as the literature shows little difference between these flow arrangements.  This procedure calculates the Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, the wall temperature correction factor (wtc) and the ratio Pitch/D_t then calls  Tube_Bundle_ND.  The procedure will determine if the flow is laminar or turbulent and apply the appropriate correlation.  Fully-developed flow is assumed.

Routines.Name: PipeFlow_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a round pipe
Routines.ShortDescription: PipeFlow_ND returns the average Nusselt number assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition in a circular tube characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, length/diameter, and relative roughness.  The procedure also returns the average friction factor for these conditions.
Routines.LongDescription:
PipeFlow_ND returns the average Nusselt number assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition in a circular tube characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, length/diameter, and relative roughness.  The procedure also returns the average friction factor for these conditions.  The procedure can be used for developing or fully-developed flow in the laminar, transitional or turbulent flow regimes.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynold's numbers between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations.  

The ratio LoverD is used to apply a developing flow correction based on simultaneous thermal and hydrodynamic development.  Set LoverD to a large number if developing flow corrections are not applicable.  Set the Prandtl number to a large value to obtain results that are consistent with thermally developing/hydrodynamically developed conditions for laminar flows.  Two Nusselt numbers are returned.  Nusselt_T corresponds to a constant temperature wall and Nusselt_H corresponds to a constant heat flux.  These two values will be the same for turbulent flow.  For laminar flow, they provide upper and lower bounds on the Nusselt number as explained in Section 5.2.4 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: DuctFlow_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a rectangular duct
Routines.ShortDescription: DuctFlow_ND returns the average Nusselt number assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition in a rectangular duct characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, length/hydraulic diameter, aspect ratio, and relative roughness.  The procedure also returns the average friction factor for these conditions.
Routines.LongDescription: DuctFlow_ND returns the average Nusselt number assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition in a rectangular duct characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, length/hydraulic diameter, aspect ratio, and relative roughness.  The procedure also returns the average friction factor for these conditions. The procedure can be used for simultaneous thermal and hydrodynamic developing flow or fully-developed flow in the laminar, transitional or turbulent flow regimes.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynolds numbers (based on hydraulic diameter) between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations.  The parameter LoverD_h is used to apply a developing flow correction if necessary.  Set LoverD_h to a large number if developing flow corrections are not applicable.  Values of L0verD_h < 0.1 are set to 0.1.  Two Nusselt numbers are returned.  Nusselt_T corresponds to a constant temperature wall and Nusselt_H corresponds to a constant heat flux.  These two values will be the same for turbulent flow.  For laminar flow, they provide upper and lower bounds on the Nusselt number as discussed in Section 5.2.4 of Nellis and Klein.  The procedure assumes simultaneous development of the thermal and hydrodynamic boundary layers; however, the results for a thermally developing/hydrodynamically developed laminar flow can be obtained by calling the procedure with a large Prandtl number.

Routines.Name: AnnularFlow_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through an annular duct
Routines.ShortDescription: AnnularFlow_ND returns the lower and upper bounds on the Nusselt number for developing or fully-developed flow in an annulus characterized by inner and outer radii.  The outer wall of the annulus is assumed to be insulated so heat transfer occurs across the wall separating the annulus from the pipe.  The area used for heat transfer should be the area of this wall.  The procedure also returns the friction factor for these conditions.
Routines.LongDescription: AnnularFlow_ND returns the lower and upper bounds on the Nusselt number for developing or fully-developed flow in an annulus characterized by inner and outer radii.  The outer wall of the annulus is assumed to be insulated so heat transfer occurs across the wall separating the annulus from the pipe.  The area used for heat transfer should be the area of this wall.  The procedure also returns the friction factor for these conditions.  The procedure will determine if the flow is laminar or turbulent.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynolds numbers (based on hydraulic diameter) between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations.  The parameter LoverD_h is used to apply a developing flow correction for the turbulent flow, if necessary.  Set LoverD_h to a large number if developing flow corrections are not applicable.  Two values of the Nusselt number coefficient are returned that should provide upper and lower bounds.  These  coefficients are both for the inner annular wall with an insulated outer wall.  They both correspond to fully developed flow. For turbulent flow, these values are identical.

Routines.Name: HelicalPipeFlow_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a pipe that is wrapped in a helix.
Routines.ShortDescription: HelicalPipeFlow_ND returns the average Nusselt number assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition in a helically wound circular tube characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, length/diameter, relative roughness, and diameter to coil radius ratio. The procedure also returns the average friction factor for these conditions.
Routines.LongDescription:
HelicalPipeFlow_ND returns the average Nusselt number assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition in a helically wound circular tube characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, length/diameter, relative roughness, and diameter to coil radius ratio. The procedure also returns the average friction factor for these conditions. The procedure also returns the average friction factor for these conditions. The procedure can be used for developing or fully-developed flow in the laminar, transitional or turbulent flow regimes. It calls PipeFlow_Laminar and PipeFlow_Turbulent to obtain the appropriate Nusselt numbers and friction factor and then modifies these straight tube results in order to account for the curvature of the coil using correlations discussed in the Heat Exchanger Design Handbook (2008) and Barron (1999).  
Two Nusselt numbers are returned. Nusselt_T corresponds to a constant temperature wall and Nusselt_H corresponds to a constant heat flux. These two values will be the same for turbulent flow. For laminar flow, they provide upper and lower bounds on the Nusselt number as explained in Section 5.2.4 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: Tube_Bundle_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Flow along a tube bundle
Routines.ShortDescription: Tube_Bundle_ND returns the average friction factor and Nusselt number for ideal longitudinal flow in a tube bundle.
Routines.LongDescription: Tube_Bundle_ND returns the average friction factor and Nusselt number for ideal longitudinal flow in a tube bundle. The correlations are applicable to flow up, down, or horizontal.  The procedure provides the correlations provided by Taborek.  It will determine if the flow is laminar or turbulent and apply the appropriate correlation based on the correlation for the transitional Reynolds number provided by El-Genk et al.

Routines.Name: PipeFlow_local
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a round pipe
Routines.ShortDescription: PipeFlow_local returns lower and upper bounds on the local heat transfer coefficient and the local pressure gradient at an axial position in a circular tube.
Routines.LongDescription: PipeFlow_local returns lower and upper bounds on the local heat transfer coefficient and the local pressure gradient at an axial position in a circular tube.  This procedure  differentiates the average heat transfer coefficient and pressure gradient provided by procedure PipeFlow.  Two values of the local heat transfer coefficient are returned.  The first, h_T_x is determined assuming that the wall is at constant temperature.  The second (h_H_x) is determined assuming that the wall is subjected to a constant heat flux.  For laminar flow, these values should provide lower and upper bounds on the heat transfer coefficient.  For turbulent flow, these values are identical.  Note that a negative mass flow will result in a positive pressure gradient evaluated at the value of x provided with x interpreted as the distance from the inlet (now the outlet) of the duct to the location of interest.  As there is no way to know how far this is from the other end of the pipe this may be inaccurate and therefore a warning is issued.

Routines.Name: HelicalPipeFlow_local
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a pipe that is wrapped in a helix.
Routines.ShortDescription: HelicalPipeFlow_local returns lower and upper bounds on the local heat transfer coefficient and the pressure gradient for a flow through a circular tube that is wound in a helix.
Routines.LongDescription: HelicalPipeFlow_local returns lower and upper bounds on the local heat transfer coefficient and the pressure gradient for a flow through a circular tube that is wound in a helix. This procedure calculates the Reynolds and Prandtl numbers and then calls the procedure HelicalPipeFlow_N.   HelicalPipeFlow_N_local calls the straight tube procedure PipeFlow_N_local and modifies the results to account for the curvature. The straight tube friction factor is modified as discussed in the Heat Exchanger Design Handbook (2008) in order to account for curvature.  The straight tube Nusselt number is modified as discussed in Barron (1999) in order to account for curvature.  Two values of the heat transfer coefficient are returned. The first, h_T is determined assuming that the wall is at constant temperature. The second is determined assuming that the wall is subjected to a constant heat flux. For laminar flow, these values should provide lower and upper bounds on the heat transfer coefficient. For turbulent flow, these values are identical.  Note that a negative mass flow will result in a positive pressure gradient evaluated at the value of x provided with x interpreted as the distance from the inlet (now the outlet) of the duct to the location of interest.  As there is no way to know how far this is from the other end of the pipe this may be inaccurate and therefore a warning is issued.

Routines.Name: zigzag_local
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a zig-zag channel
Routines.ShortDescription: ZigZag_local returns the local (averaged over a unit cell) heat transfer coefficient and pressure gradient associated with flow through a zig-zag channel.  The procedure also provides the local Nusselt number, local friction factor, and Reynolds number (entrance effects are not included - these are local in that they are at a particular location)
Routines.LongDescription: ZigZag_local returns the local (averaged over a unit cell) heat transfer coefficient and pressure gradient associated with flow through a zig-zag channel.  The procedure also provides the local Nusselt number, local friction factor, and Reynolds number (entrance effects are not included - these are local in that they are at a particular location).  Note that a negative value of mass flow rate leads to a positive pressure gradient.  This procedure uses the correlation from Moisseytsev et al. (2020).

Routines.Name: PipeFlow_ND_local
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a round pipe
Routines.ShortDescription: PipeFlow_ND_local returns the local Nusselt numbers assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition a circular tube characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers,axial position/diameter, and relative roughness.  The procedure also returns the local friction factor for these conditions.
Routines.LongDescription: PipeFlow_ND_local returns the local Nusselt numbers assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition a circular tube characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers,axial position/diameter, and relative roughness.  The procedure also returns the local friction factor for these conditions.  The procedure can be used for developing or fully-developed flow in the laminar, transitional or turbulent flow regimes.  This procedure  determines the local Nusselt numbers and friction factor by differentiating the average values provided by the PipeFlow_ND procedure.  See PipeFlow_ND{linkID=1020} for more information. The Nusselt numbers approach infinity as xoverD goes to 0.  The correlations are not applicable for xoverD ratios less than 0.1.  Two Nusselt numbers are returned.  Nusselt_T corresponds to a constant temperature wall and Nusselt_H corresponds to a constant heat flux.  These two values will be the same for turbulent flow.  For laminar flow, they provide upper and lower bounds on the Nusselt number.

Routines.Name: DuctFlow_ND_local
Routines.DisplayName: Internal flow through a rectangular duct
Routines.ShortDescription: DuctFlow_ND_local returns the local Nusselt number assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition in a rectangular duct characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, local position/hydraulic diameter, aspect ratio, and relative roughness.  The procedure also returns the friction factor for these conditions.
Routines.LongDescription:
DuctFlow_ND_local returns the local Nusselt number assuming constant temperature wall and constant heat flux for a given flow condition in a rectangular duct characterized by Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, local position/hydraulic diameter, aspect ratio, and relative roughness.  The procedure also returns the friction factor for these conditions.   The procedure can be used for simultaneous thermal and hydrodynamic developing flow or fully-developed flow in the laminar, transitional or turbulent flow regimes.  This procedure calls DuctFlow_N{linkID=1120} to obtain the average Nusselt numbers and friction factor.  See that routine or Section 5.2.4 of Nellis and Klein for additional information.  Two Nusselt numbers are returned.  Nusselt_T_x corresponds to a constant temperature wall and Nusselt_H_x corresponds to a constant heat flux.  These two values will be the same for turbulent flow.  For laminar flow, they provide upper and lower bounds on the Nusselt number.  The procedure assumes simultaneous development of the thermal and hydrodynamic boundary layers; however, the results for a thermally developing/hydrodynamically developed condition can be obtained by calling the procedure with a large Prandtl number.

If  xoverD is less than 0.1, it is set to 0.1..

Routines.Name: HelicalPipeFlow_ND_local

Two Nusselt numbers are returned. Nusselt_T corresponds to a constant temperature wall and Nusselt_H corresponds to a constant heat flux. These two values will be the same for turbulent flow. For laminar flow, they provide upper and lower bounds on the Nusselt number as explained in Section 5.2.4 of  Nellis and Klein

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Sphere
