Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Sphere calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force and coefficient for external flow past a sphere.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Sphere calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force and coefficient for external flow past a sphere.  The correlation is from White (1991) and Nellis and Klein.  This procedure passes the Reynold and Prandtl numbers to the non-dimensional procedure External_Flow_Sphere_ND. The non-dimensional procedure returns the values for C_d and Nusselt.   External_Flow_Sphere calculates the drag force and the heat transfer coefficient for convection from the drag coefficient and the Nusselt number,

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Cylinder
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Cylinder calculates the average heat transfer coefficient, drag force per unit length of cylinder and the drag coefficient for external flow past an infinite cylinder.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Cylinder calculates the average heat transfer coefficient, drag force per unit length of cylinder and the drag coefficient for external flow past an infinite cylinder.  The procedure uses the correlation presented in White (1991) and Section 4.9.3 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Cuboid
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a cuboid
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Cuboid calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force for external flow past a cuboid.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Cuboid calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force for external flow past a cuboid.  The drag coefficient correlation is obtained from Haider and Levenspiel (1989) while the Nusselt number correlation is obtained from Yovanovich (1988).

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Plate
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a flat plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Plate calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and the average shear stress for external flow over a flat plate.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Plate calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and the average shear stress for external flow over a flat plate. This procedure determines the property data of the specified fluid and calculates the Reynolds and Prandtl numbers. The Prandtl, Reynolds and Nusselt numbers are based on the film temperature, which is the average of the free stream and the surface temperatures.  This procedure then passes the Reynolds and Prandtl numbers to the non-dimensional procedure External_Flow_Plate_ND. The non-dimensional procedure then returns the values for C_f and Nusselt and External_Flow_Plate calculates the average shear stress and the convection heat transfer coefficient.  Note that the procedure External_Flow_Plate_L provides the same functionality but uses the more accurate correlations described by Lienhard (2020) that include the impact of the transition region.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Plate_local
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a flat plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Plate_local calculates the local heat transfer coefficient and the local shear stress for external flow over a flat plate.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Plate_local calculates the local heat transfer coefficient and the local shear stress for external flow over a flat plate.  This procedure determines the property data of the specified fluid and calculates the Reynolds and Prandtl numbers. The Prandtl, Reynolds and Nusselt numbers are based on the film temperature, which is the average of the free stream and the surface temperatures.  This procedure then passes the Reynolds and Prandtl numbers to the non-dimensional procedure External_Flow_Plate_ND_local. The non-dimensional procedure then returns the values for C_f and Nusselt and External_Flow_Plate_local calculates the local shear stress and the convection heat transfer coefficient.  Note that the procedure External_Flow_Plate_L_local provides the same functionality but uses the more accurate correlations described by Lienhard (2020) that include the impact of the transition region.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Plate_L
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a flat plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Plate_L calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and the average shear stress for external flow over a flat plate.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Plate_L calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and the average shear stress for external flow over a flat plate.  The results returned use the Lienhard (2020) correlation which accounts for the transition region.  This procedure uses the non-dimensional procedure External_Flow_Plate_L_ND with an assumed transition Reynolds number of Re_l 1e5. The non-dimensional procedure then returns the values for C_f and Nusselt and External_Flow_Plate calculates the average shear stress and the convection heat transfer coefficient.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Plate_L_local
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a flat plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Plate_L_local calculates the local heat transfer coefficient and the local shear stress for external flow over a flat plate.   The correlation provided by Lienhard (2020) is used which accounts for the presence of the transition region; a transition Reynolds number of Re_l = 1e5 is assumed.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Plate_L_local calculates the local heat transfer coefficient and the local shear stress for external flow over a flat plate.   The correlation provided by Lienhard (2020) is used which accounts for the presence of the transition region; a transition Reynolds number of Re_l = 1e5 is assumed.  This procedure uses the non-dimensional procedure External_Flow_Plate_L_ND_local with an assumed value of Re_l = 1e5. The non-dimensional procedure then returns the values for C_f and Nusselt and External_Flow_Plate_L_local calculates the local shear stress and the convection heat transfer coefficient.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Inline_Bank
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over an inline bank of tubes
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Inline_Bank calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and total pressure drop over an inline bank of tubes.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Inline_Bank calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and total pressure drop over an inline bank of tubes. The procedure uses correlations and correction factors provided by Zukauskas (1972). These correlations apply for values of Reynolds numbers from 30<Re<1e8 and Prandtl numbers from 0.7<Pr<500.  At Reynolds numbers 100<Re<1000, the heat transfer coefficient can be calculated assuming a single cylinder in crossflow. Under those conditions the Churchill and Bernstein correlation(1977) is used.  Experimental data verifying the correlations are limited in geometric layout to relative longitudinal pitches (S_L/D) between 1.25 and 2.5.  The accuracy of values outside this range is uncertain.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Staggered_Bank
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a staggered bank of tubes
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Staggered_Bank calculates the average heat transfer coefficient, and total pressure drop over a staggered bank of tubes.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Staggered_Bank calculates the average heat transfer coefficient, and total pressure drop over a staggered bank of tubes.  The procedure uses correlations and correction factors provided by Zukauskas (1972). These correlations apply for values of Reynolds numbers from 30<Re<1e8 and Prandtl numbers from 0.7<Pr<500. At Reynolds numbers 100<Re<1000, the coefficient of heat transfer can be calculated assuming a single cylinder in crossflow. Under those conditions the Churchill and Bernstein correlation(1977) is used. Experimental data verifying the correlations are limited in geometric layout to relative transverse pitches (S_T/D) between 1.25 and 2.5. The accuracy of values outside this range is uncertain.

Routines.Name: external_flow_finned_bank1
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over an inline bank of finned tubes.
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Finned_Bank1 calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and total pressure drop over an inline bank of finned tubes.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Finned_Bank1 calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and total pressure drop over an inline bank of finned tubes.  The procedure uses correlations and correction factors for pressure drop provided by Yudin and Tokhtarova (1974) as presented in the Heat Exchanger Design Handbook (2008).  The correlation for heat transfer is from PFR (2008).  The correlations for pressure drop apply from 4e3< Re< 1.6e5.

Routines.Name: external_flow_finned_bank2
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over an staggered bank of finned tubes.
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Finned_Bank2 calculates the average heat transfer coefficient, and total pressure drop over a staggered bank of finned tubes.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Finned_Bank2 calculates the average heat transfer coefficient, and total pressure drop over a staggered bank of finned tubes.  The procedure uses correlations and correction factors for pressure drop provided by Yudin and Tokhtarova (1974) as presented in the Heat Exchanger Design Handbook (2008).  The correlation for heat transfer is from PFR (2008).  The correlations for pressure drop apply from Re> 2.2e3.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Diamond
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a diamond shaped extrusion
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Diamond calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force per unit length of a diamond-shaped extrusion.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Diamond calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force per unit length of a diamond-shaped extrusion.  Uses correlation from  Jakob (1949), White (2003) and Nellis and Klein (2009).

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Square
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a square shaped extrusion
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Square calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force per unit length of a square-shaped extrusion.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Square calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force per unit length of a square-shaped extrusion. Uses correlation from  Jakob (1949), White (2003) and Nellis and Klein (2009).

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Hexagon1
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a hexagon shaped extrusion
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Hexagon1 calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force per unit length of a hexagonal-shaped extrusion (with the flat face perpendicular to the flow).
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Hexagon1 calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force per unit length of a hexagonal-shaped rod (with the flat face perpendicular to the flow).  Uses correlation from Jakob (1949) and White (2003).

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Hexagon2
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a hexagon shaped extrusion
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Hexagon2 calculates the average heat transfer coefficient, drag force per unit length of a hexagonal-shaped extrusion (with the flat face parallel to the flow)
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Hexagon2 calculates the average heat transfer coefficient, drag force per unit length of a hexagonal-shaped extrusion (with the flat face parallel to the flow). Uses correlation from Jakob (1949) and White (2003).

Routines.Name: External_Flow_VerticalPlate
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over an extruded vertical plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_VerticalPlate calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force per unit length of vertical plate
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_VerticalPlate calculates the average heat transfer coefficient and drag force per unit length of vertical plate.  Uses correlation from Jakob (1949) and White (2003).

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Sphere_ND
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a sphere
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Sphere_ND returns the average Nusselt number and the drag coefficient for a sphere in crossflow.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Sphere_ND returns the average Nusselt number and the drag coefficient for a sphere in crossflow. This procedure is called by External_Flow_Sphere to calculate the Nusselt number and drag coefficient. The procedure uses the Whitaker correlation (Whitaker, S., AICHE J., Vol. 18, 361, 1972) as reported in Mills, A.F. Basic Heat and Mass Transfer, Irwin, 1995 and presented in Nellis and Klein.  The correlation is valid for Re<7.6E4. The coefficient of drag uses the correlation presented by White (1991).  Data for the coefficient of drag are available for Reynolds numbers up to 2E5.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Cylinder_ND
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Cylinder_ND returns the average Nusselt number and the drag coefficient for an isothermal cylinder in crossflow.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Cylinder_ND returns the average Nusselt number and the drag coefficient for an isothermal cylinder in crossflow. This procedure is called by External_Flow_Cylinder to calculate the Nusselt number and drag coefficient. The procedure uses the Churchill and Bernstein correlation(1977) as described in Nellis and Klein.  It has been validated at all tested Reynolds numbers with Re*Pr>0.2. The coefficient of drag is based on the correlation presented in White (1991). Data for the coefficient of drag are available for Reynolds numbers up to 1E7.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Plate_ND
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a flat plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Plate_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow parallel to a flat plate.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Plate_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow parallel to a flat plate.  This procedure is called by External_Flow_Plate to calculate the Nusselt number and average shear stress.  The procedure uses the correlations for average C_f and average Nusselt number provided by Nellis and Klein (2018).  Note that the procedure External_Flow_Plate_L_ND provides the same functionality but uses the more accurate correlations described by Lienhard (2020) that include the impact of the transition region.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Plate_ND_local
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a flat plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Plate_ND_local returns the local Nusselt number and local friction coefficient for flow parallel to a flat plate.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Plate_ND_local returns the local Nusselt number and local friction coefficient for flow parallel to a flat plate.  This procedure uses the correlations presented in Nellis and Klein (2018) to determine the local Nusselt number and friction coefficient.  Note that the procedure External_Flow_Plate_L_ND_local provides the same functionality but uses the more accurate correlations described by Lienhard (2020) that include the impact of the transition region.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Plate_L_ND
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a flat plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Plate_L_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow parallel to a flat plate.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Plate_L_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow parallel to a flat plate using the correlation provided by Lienhard (2020) which considers the transition region.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Plate_L_ND_local
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a flat plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Plate_L_ND_local returns the local Nusselt number and local friction coefficient for flow parallel to a flat plate.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Plate_L_ND_local returns the local Nusselt number and local friction coefficient for flow parallel to a flat plate using the correlation provided by Lienhard (2020) which considers the transition region.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Diamond_ND
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a diamond shaped extrusion
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Diamond_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past an infinitely long diamond-shaped extrusion.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Diamond_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past an infinitely long diamond-shaped extrusion. The correlation for Nusselt number is valid for 5E3<Re<1E5 as indicated in Table 4-7 of Nellis and Klein.  The correlation for the drag coefficient is valid for Re>1E4.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Square_ND
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a square shaped extrusion
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Square_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past a infinitely long square-shaped extrusion.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Square_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past a infinitely long square-shaped extrusion. The correlation for Nusselt number is valid for 5E3<Re<1E5.  The correlation for the drag coefficient is valid for Re>1E4

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Hexagon1_ND
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a hexagon shaped extrusion
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Hexagon1_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past a infinitely long hexagon-shaped extrusion with the flat-edge perpendicular to the flow, as shown.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Hexagon1_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past a infinitely long hexagon-shaped extrusion with the flat-edge perpendicular to the flow.  The correlation for Nusselt number is valid for 5E3<Re<1E5 as described in Table 4-7 of Nellis and Klein.  The correlation for the drag coefficient is valid for Re>1E4.

Routines.Name: External_Flow_Hexagon2_ND
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over a hexagon shaped extrusion
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_Hexagon2_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past a infinitely long hexagon-shaped rod with the flat-edge parallel to the flow.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_Hexagon2_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past a infinitely long hexagon-shaped rod with the flat-edge parallel to the flow. The correlation for Nusselt number is valid for 5E3<Re<1E5 as noted in Table 4-7 of Nellis and Klein.  The correlation for the drag coefficient is valid for Re>1E4

Routines.Name: External_Flow_VerticalPlate_ND
Routines.DisplayName: External flow over an extruded vertical plate
Routines.ShortDescription: External_Flow_VerticalPlate_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past a infinitely long vertical plate of height W.
Routines.LongDescription: External_Flow_VerticalPlate_ND returns the average Nusselt number and friction coefficient for flow past a infinitely long vertical plate of height W. The correlation for Nusselt number is valid for 4E3<Re<1.5E4 as described in .  The correlation for the drag coefficient is valid for Re>1E4.

Routines.Name: FC_Tilted_Rect_Enclosure
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection in a rectangular enclosure
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_Tilted_Rect_Enclosure returns the heat transfer coefficient in a rectangular channel that is tilted with respect to horizontal.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_Tilted_Rect_Enclosure returns the heat transfer coefficient in a rectangular channel that is tilted with respect to horizontal.  The correlation is from Hollands et al. (1976).  For angles >70 deg, the correlation is modified according to  Catton(1975) as described in section 6.2.6 of Nellis and Klein.  The ratio of the channel width to delta is assumed to be > 12.  Also, L/delta should be >12 for the correlation to be applicable.

Routines.Name: FC_plate_vertical
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a vertical plate
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_plate_vertical returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for a vertical flat plate (heated or cooled).
Routines.LongDescription: FC_plate_vertical returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for a vertical flat plate (heated or cooled).  The correlation is described in section 6.2.2 of Nellis and Klein.  The width of the plate is assumed sufficiently large such that end effects may be neglected.

Routines.Name: FC_plate_horizontal1
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a heated upward-facing horizontal plate
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_horizontal1 returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for a horizontal flat plate that is upward heated or downward cooled.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_horizontal1 returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for a horizontal flat plate that is upward heated or downward cooled. The characteristic length of the plate is the ratio of the area to the perimeter.  The procedure FC_plate_horizontal1_ND is called to calculate the Nusselt number. FC_plate_horizontal1, in turn, uses the Nusselt number to calculate the coefficient of heat transfer as described in Section 6.2.2 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: FC_plate_horizontal2
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a cooled upward-facing plate
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_horizontal1 returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for a horizontal flat plate that is upward heated or downward cooled.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_horizontal1 returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for a horizontal flat plate that is upward heated or downward cooled. The characteristic length of the plate is the ratio of the area to the perimeter.  The non-dimensional procedure FC_plate_horizontal2_ND is called to calculate the Nusselt number. FC_plate_horizontal2, in turn, uses the Nusselt number to calculate the coefficient of heat transfer as described in Section 6.2.2 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: FC_plate_tilted
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a tilted heated plate
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_plate_tilted returns the heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number for a tilted flat plate (heated or cooled) that is tilted with respect to horizontal.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_plate_tilted returns the heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number for a tilted flat plate (heated or cooled) that is tilted with respect to horizontal.  The width of the plate is assumed sufficiently large such that end effects may be neglected. This function implements the method of Raithby and Hollands (1998) that uses the horizontal and vertical plate correlations to estimate the heat transfer from a heated plate inclined at an arbitrary angle, 0 < z < 180 degree, as described in Section 6.2.2 of Nellis and Klein.  The function is specifically coded for a heated plate (i.e., T_s>T_infinity).  However, if T_s<T_infinity, the function internally changes the tilt to be 180-tilt.  The net result is that the heat transfer coefficient for a cooled plate facing up is the same as for a heated plate facing down.

Routines.Name: FC_sphere
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a sphere
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_sphere returns the heat transfer coefficient for an isothermal sphere submerged in a fluid and subjected to gravity.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_sphere returns the heat transfer coefficient for an isothermal sphere submerged in a fluid and subjected to gravity. The non-dimensional procedure FC_sphere_ND is called to calculate the Nusselt number. FC_sphere, in turn, uses the Nusselt number to calculate the coefficient of heat transfer as described in Section 6.2.3 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: FC_horizontal_cylinder
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a horizontal cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_horizontal_cylinder returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for an infinitely long horizontal cylinder.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_horizontal_cylinder returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for an infinitely long horizontal cylinder. In practice, the cylinder need only be long enough so that the end effects are negligible (~L/D = 5). The non-dimensional procedure FC_horizontal_cylinder_ND is called to calculate the Nusselt number. FC_horizontal_cylinder, in turn, uses the Nusselt number to calculate the heat transfer coefficient as described in Section 6.2.4 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: FC_vertical_cylinder
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a vertical cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_vertical_cylinder returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for an vertical cylinder.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_vertical_cylinder returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for an vertical cylinder.  The non-dimensional procedure FC_vertical_cylinder_ND is called to calculate the Nusselt number as described in Section 6.2.4 of Nellis and Klein. FC_vertical_cylinder, in turn, uses the Nusselt number to calculate the coefficient of heat transfer.

Routines.Name: FC_Vertical_Channel
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a vertical heated channel
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_vertical_channel returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for an vertical open channel .
Routines.LongDescription: FC_vertical_channel returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number and Rayleigh number for an vertical open channel. The non-dimensional procedure FC_Vertical_Channel_ND is called to calculate the Nusselt number. FC_vertical_channel, in turn, uses the Nusselt number to calculate the coefficient of heat transfer in the manner described in Section 6.2.5 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: FC_Annular_Enclosure
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection within a horizontal annular space
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_Annular_Enclosure returns the heat transfer coefficient in an annular space that is formed between two concentric horizontal cylinders.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_Annular_Enclosure returns the heat transfer coefficient in an annular space that is formed between two concentric horizontal cylinders.  Note that the area of the inner cylinder should be used when computing heat transfer rate.  The correlation that is used is from Barron and Nellis, Cryogenic Heat Transfer, 2nd Edition, CRC Press, 2016.

Routines.Name: FC_Horizontal_Cylinder_Bank
Routines.DisplayName: Provides standard pipe dimensions
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_Horizontal_Cylinder_Bank returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number, and Raleigh number associated with free convection for a vertically aligned bank of horizontal cylinders.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_Horizontal_Cylinder_Bank returns the heat transfer coefficient, Nusselt number, and Raleigh number associated with free convection for a vertically aligned bank of horizontal cylinders.  The correlation that is used is from Kitmura et al. (2016).  The procedure computes the ratio of the Nusselt number for the Nth cylinder from the bottom of a heated bank (or from the top of a cooled bank) relative to the first cylinder and then applies this ratio to the Nusselt number calculated for a single horizontal cylinder in free convection using the procedure FC_horizontal_cylinder_ND.  In this way the results are consistent with the single cylinder results as N goes to 1.  In addition to the heat transfer coefficient, the procedure returns the Nusselt number (based on diameter) and Raleigh number (based on diameter and temperature difference).  These dimensionless numbers are therefore consistent with those used in other procedures for free convection even though the definitions found in Kimura et al. (2016) are different.

Routines.Name: FC_Tilted_Rect_Enclosure_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection in a rectangular enclosure
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_Tilted_Rect_Enclosure_N returns the Nusselt number in a rectangular channel that is tilted with respect to horizontal.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_Tilted_Rect_Enclosure_N returns the Nusselt number in a rectangular channel that is tilted with respect to horizontal.  The correlation is from Hollands et al. (1976).  For angles >70 deg, the correlation is modified according to  Catton (1975) as reported in Section 6.2.6 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: FC_plate_vertical_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a vertical plate
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_plate_vertical_ND returns the Nusselt number for a vertical flat plate (heated or cooled) given the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_plate_vertical_ND returns the Nusselt number for a vertical flat plate (heated or cooled) given the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers. The Rayleigh number should be calculated based on the length L in the direction of gravity. The width of the plate is assumed sufficiently large such that end effects may be neglected.  The correlation in procedure FC_plate_vertical_ND is from Churchill and Chu (1975b).  The correlation is valid from 0.1<Ra<1e12.

Routines.Name: FC_plate_horizontal1_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a heated upward-facing horizontal plate
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_plate_horizontal1_ND returns the Nusselt number for a heated horizontal upward facing flat plate or a cooled downward facing flat plate given the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers. The Rayleigh number should be calculated based on a length scale defined as the ratio of the surface area of the plate to its perimeter.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_plate_horizontal1_ND returns the Nusselt number for a heated horizontal upward facing flat plate or a cooled downward facing flat plate given the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers. The Rayleigh number should be calculated based on a length scale defined as the ratio of the surface area of the plate to its perimeter.  The procedure FC_plate_horizontal1_ND is based on a compilation of correlations listed in Handbook of Heat Transfer, Third Ed. on pages 4.8-4.19 as described in Section 6.2.2 of Nellis and Klein. These correlations include and weight the Nusselt number contributions from the laminar and turbulent boundary layers. The correlation is valid from 1<Ra<1e10.

Routines.Name: FC_plate_horizontal2_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a cooled upward-facing plate
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_plate_horizontal2_ND returns the Nusselt number for a heated horizontal downward facing flat plate or a cooled upward facing flat plate given the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers. The Rayleigh number should be calculated based on a length scale defined as the ratio of the surface area of the plate to its perimeter.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_plate_horizontal2_ND returns the Nusselt number for a heated horizontal downward facing flat plate or a cooled upward facing flat plate given the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers. The Rayleigh number should be calculated based on a length scale defined as the ratio of the surface area of the plate to its perimeter. The procedure FC_plate_horizontal2_ND is based on a compilation of correlations listed in Handbook of Heat Transfer, Third Ed. on pages 4.8-4.19 as reported in Section 6.2.2 of Nellis and Klein. The correlation assumes laminar flow and is valid from 1000<Ra<1e10.

Routines.Name: FC_sphere_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a sphere
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_sphere_ND returns the Nusselt number for a sphere (heated or cooled) immersed in a fluid, given a characteristic Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_sphere_ND returns the Nusselt number for a sphere (heated or cooled) immersed in a fluid, given a characteristic Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers. The procedure FC_sphere_ND is based on the Churchill (1983) correlation as described in Section 6.2.3 of Nellis and Klein. This correlation is valid for Pr>~0.7 and Ra<~1e11.

Routines.Name: FC_horizontal_cylinder_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a horizontal cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_horizontal_cylinder_ND returns the Nusselt number for a horizontal cylinder immersed in a fluid.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_horizontal_cylinder_ND returns the Nusselt number for a horizontal cylinder immersed in a fluid. The procedure uses the correlation provided by Churchill and Chu (1975). This correlation is valid for all Pr and 1e-10<Ra<1e12.

Routines.Name: FC_vertical_cylinder_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Free convection from a vertical cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: FC_vertical_cylinder_ND returns the Nusselt number for a vertical cylinder immersed in a fluid given the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers and L\D ratio.
Routines.LongDescription: FC_vertical_cylinder_ND returns the Nusselt number for a vertical cylinder immersed in a fluid given the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers and L\D ratio. The Rayleigh number should be calculated based on the length L.  The procedure is based off of two distinct correlations. For D\L ratios that are sufficiently large, as defined by Sparrow and Gregg (1956), the cylinder can be approximated by a vertical plate of length L. The Nusselt number can then be determined by use of the FC_plate_ND procedure. For values of D\L that are small, the Nusselt number can be found through the correlation on page 4.18-4.20 in the Handbook of Heat Transfer as described in Section 6.2.4 of Nellis and Klein. The above correlations are valid for 1<Ra<1e11.

Routines.Name: FC_Vertical_Channel_ND

Routines.Name: SpheresPacking
Routines.DisplayName: Flow through a packed bed of spheres
Routines.ShortDescription: SpheresPacking returns the fluid side behavior of a packed matrix of spheres.
Routines.LongDescription: SpheresPacking returns the fluid side behavior of a packed matrix of spheres.  This function determines the fluid properties at the stated pressure and temperature, and the Reynolds number from the sphere diameter. The non-dimensional function PackedSpheres_ND is called to determine the values for the Colburn j and friction factor. The Colburn j factor is interpreted by PackedSpheres and returned as a heat transfer coefficient.  The porosity for a theoretically perfect spherical matrix, i.e., all the spheres are exactly the same diameter and are packed as close as possible, is 0.30 but porosity usually ranges from 0.32 to 0.37.  The core pressure drop is determined based on frictional considerations. The total pressure drop also includes fluid acceleration.

Routines.Name: ScreensPacking
Routines.DisplayName: Flow through a packed bed of screens
Routines.ShortDescription: ScreensPacking returns the flow-side behavior of a randomly stacked array of woven screens.
Routines.LongDescription: ScreensPacking returns the flow-side behavior of a randomly stacked array of woven screens.  This function determines the fluid properties at the average pressure and temperature, and the Reynold's number from the screen mesh and wire diameter. In order to determine the Reynold's number, the porosity is needed. The idealized equations relating the screen mesh and diameter to porosity were based on those provided on page 52 of Ackermann (1997). With the Reynold's number and porosity calculated, the non-dimensional function Screens_ND is called to determine the values for the Colburn j and friction factor using either the correlation selected. The Colburn j factor is interpreted by Screens and returned as a heat transfer coefficient. It is assumed that the screens are perfectly arranged, i.e. the thickness of a single screen is exactly twice the wire diameter, and there is no gap between successive screens.  The core pressure drop is determined based on frictional considerations. Pressure drop due to fluid acceleration and expansion/contraction are included in DELTAp but not in DELTAp_c.

Routines.Name: TrianglesPacking
Routines.DisplayName: Flow through a packed bed of triangular channels
Routines.ShortDescription: TrianglesPacking returns the fluid side behavior of a matrix comprised of triangular passages.
Routines.LongDescription: TrianglesPacking returns the fluid side behavior of a matrix comprised of triangular passages. This function determines the fluid properties at the stated pressure and temperature, and the Reynolds number from the hydraulic diameter. Then the non-dimensional function Triangular_Channel_ND is called to determine the values for the Colburn j and friction factor. The Colburn j factor is interpreted and returned as a heat transfer coefficient. Data from Kays and London are used. The core pressure drop includes only frictional effect.  The total pressure drop also includes entrance and exit losses and fluid acceleration.

Routines.Name: Impinging_Jet_SRN
Routines.DisplayName: Single round nozzle
Routines.ShortDescription: Impinging_Jets_SRN calculates the average heat transfer and Nusselt number for a single round nozzle (SRN) jet with diameter D positioned perpendicular to a plate with its exit a distance H from the plate.  The heat transfer coefficient is averaged over an area of the plate with radius r concentric with the nozzle.
Routines.LongDescription: Impinging_Jets_SRN calculates the average heat transfer and Nusselt number for a single round nozzle (SRN) jet with diameter D positioned perpendicular to a plate with its exit a distance H from the plate.  The heat transfer coefficient is averaged over an area of the plate with radius r concentric with the nozzle. This procedure is responsible for determining the property data of the fluid specified and calculating the Reynold and Prandtl numbers. This procedure then passes dimensionless information to the non-dimensional procedure Impinging_Jets_SRN_ND. The non-dimensional procedure returns the values for  Nusselt number which is used to calculate the heat transfer coefficient.

Routines.Name: Impinging_Jet_ASN_ND

Routines.Name: eta_fin_straight_rect
Routines.DisplayName: Fin efficiency for a straight fin with a rectangular base
Routines.ShortDescription: Eta_fin_straight_rect calculates the fin efficiency of a straight fin with a rectangular base.
Routines.LongDescription: Eta_fin_straight_rect calculates the fin efficiency of a straight fin with a rectangular base. This function is applicable for a fin where W>>th (i.e., the fin is infinitely long into the page).  To account for the convection from the tip, the function uses a corrected length and then calls eta_fin_straight_rect_ND.

Routines.Name: eta_fin_straight_triangular
Routines.DisplayName: Fin efficiency for a fin tapered to a point
Routines.ShortDescription: Eta_fin_straight_triangular calculates the fin efficiency of a triangular fin with a rectangular base.
Routines.LongDescription: Eta_fin_straight_triangular calculates the fin efficiency of a triangular fin with a rectangular base.  The fin is infinitely wide.  Function uses eta_fin_straight_triangular_ND.

Routines.Name: eta_fin_straight_parabolic
Routines.DisplayName: Fin efficiency for a parabolic fin tapered to a point
Routines.ShortDescription: Eta_fin_straight_parabolic calculates the fin efficiency of a concave parabolic fin with a rectangular base.
Routines.LongDescription: Eta_fin_straight_parabolic calculates the fin efficiency of a concave parabolic fin with a rectangular base. The fin is infinitely wide.  Function uses eta_fin_straight_parabolic_ND.

Routines.Name: eta_fin_straight_parabolic2
Routines.DisplayName: Fin efficiency for a parabolic fin tapered to a point
Routines.ShortDescription: Eta_fin_straight_parabolic2 calculates the fin efficiency of a convex parabolic fin with a rectangular base.
Routines.LongDescription: Eta_fin_straight_parabolic2 calculates the fin efficiency of a convex parabolic fin with a rectangular base. The fin is infinitely wide.  Function uses eta_fin_straight_parabolic2_ND.

Routines.Name: eta_fin_spine_rect
Routines.DisplayName: Fin efficiency for a cylindrical fin

Routines.LongDescription: Eta_fin_spine_triangular calculates the fin efficiency of a triangular fin with a circular base.  Function calls eta_fin_spine_triangular_ND.

Routines.LongDescription: Eta_fin_spine_parabolic calculates the fin efficiency of a concave parabolic fin with a circular base.  Function calls eta_fin_spine_parabolic_ND.

Routines.Name: eta_fin_constantCS

Routines.DisplayName: Fin efficiency for a straight fin with a rectangular base
Routines.ShortDescription: Eta_fin_straight_rect_ND returns the fin efficiency of a straight fin with a rectangular base given the product of the fin parameter, m, and fin length, L.

Routines.Name: verticalupward1
Routines.DisplayName: Flow regime map for vertical upward two-phase flow.
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a vertical upward two phase flow based on the work by Hewitt and Roberts (1969).
Routines.LongDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a vertical upward two phase flow based on the work by Hewitt and Roberts (1969).  The axes are gas density x superficial gas velocity^2 (y-axis) and liquid density x superficial liquid velocity^2 (x-axis).

Routines.Name: verticalupward2
Routines.DisplayName: Flow regime map for vertical upward two-phase flow.
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a vertical upward two phase flow based on the work by Taitel et al. (1980).
Routines.LongDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a vertical upward two phase flow based on the work by Taitel et al. (1980).  The specific flow map shown is for an air-water mixture at room temperature and pressure in a 5 cm tube.   The axes are superficial gas velocity (y-axis) and superficial liquid velocity (x-axis).

Routines.Name: verticalupward3
Routines.DisplayName: Flow regime map for vertical upward two-phase flow.
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides an EES tab allowing the development of a flow map for vertical upward two phase flow.
Routines.LongDescription: A Toolbox Tab is available that implements the equations provided by Taitel et al. (1980) to create the flow regime map for a vertical upward two phase flow.  The toolbox tab can be used if you have a Professional License of EES by downloading the .eestab file from the fchart website at: https://fchartsoftware.com/ees/toolboxtabs.php and then opening by selecting Open Tab when you right-click on one of the tabs.    The specific flow map obtained by Vertical Upward Flow Map 2 is for an air-water mixture at room temperature and pressure in a 5 cm tube.  The Toolbox Tab can be used to make a flow map that is relevant to any fluid and condition for a given tube geometry.

Routines.Name: horizontal1

Routines.ShortDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a horizontal two phase flow based on the work by Baker (1954).
Routines.LongDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a horizontal two phase flow based on the work by Baker (1954).

Routines.Name: horizontal2
Routines.DisplayName: Flow regime map for a horizontal two phase flow
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a horizontal two phase flow based on the work by Mandhane (1974).
Routines.LongDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a horizontal two phase flow based on the work by Mandhane (1974).   The axes are superficial gas velocity (y-axis) and superficial liquid velocity (x-axis).

Routines.Name: horizontal3
Routines.DisplayName: Flow regime map for a horizontal two phase flow
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a horizontal two phase flow based on the work by Govier and Aziz (1972).
Routines.LongDescription: Provides a plot showing the flow regime map for a horizontal two phase flow based on the work by Govier and Aziz (1972).  Map is for the flow of air and water in a 2.6 cm tube.   The axes are superficial gas velocity (y-axis) and superficial liquid velocity (x-axis).

Routines.Name: verticaljet1

Routines.ShortDescription: Provides a plot showing the dimensionless centerline velocity for a vertical buoyant jet based on the work by Chen and Chen (1979).

Routines.Name: HX_counterflow
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a counter flow heat exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the counter flow heat exchanger configuration.
Routines.LongDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the counter flow heat exchanger configuration.  The counterflow configuration requires that the two fluids flow in opposite directions.  Solution is from Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: HX_parallelflow
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a parallel flow heat exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the parallel flow heat exchanger configuration.
Routines.LongDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the parallel flow heat exchanger configuration.  The parallel configuration requires that the two fluids flow in the same directions.  Solution is from Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: HX_crossflow_both_unmixed
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a crossflow heat exchanger with both fluids unmixed
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the crossflow flow heat exchanger configuration with both fluids unmixed.
Routines.LongDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the crossflow flow heat exchanger configuration with both fluids mixed.  The cross flow heat exchanger configuration requires that the two fluids flow perpendicular to each other.  The unmixed configuration indicates that the fluid cannot mix with itself across the width of the heat exchanger as it flows; practically, this means that the fluid can support a temperature gradient in the direction perpendicular to the flow direction.  Solution is from Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: HX_crossflow_one_unmixed
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a crossflow heat exchanger with one fluid unmixed
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the crossflow flow heat exchanger configuration with one fluid unmixed and the other mixed.
Routines.LongDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the crossflow flow heat exchanger configuration with one fluid unmixed and the other mixed.  The cross flow heat exchanger configuration requires that the two fluids flow perpendicular to each other.  The unmixed configuration indicates that the fluid cannot mix with itself across the width of the heat exchanger as it flows; practically, this means that the fluid can support a temperature gradient in the direction perpendicular to the flow direction.  The mixed configuration indicates that the fluid can mix with itself across the width of the heat exchanger as it flows; practically, this means that the fluid cannot support a temperature gradient in the direction perpendicular to the flow direction. Solution is from Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: HX_crossflow_both_mixed
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a crossflow heat exchanger with both fluids mixed
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the crossflow flow heat exchanger configuration with both fluids mixed.
Routines.LongDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for the crossflow flow heat exchanger configuration with both fluids mixed.  The cross flow heat exchanger configuration requires that the two fluids flow perpendicular to each other.  The mixed configuration indicates that the fluid can mix with itself across the width of the heat exchanger as it flows; practically, this means that the fluid cannot support a temperature gradient in the direction perpendicular to the flow direction. Solution is from Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: HX_shell&tube_1
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a shell and tube heat exchanger with 1 shell pass and 2 tube passes.
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a shell and tube heat exchanger with 1 shell pass and 2 tube passes.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 1-2 TEMA E shell and tube heat exchanger has an E type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at one end and leaves at the other.  It consists of one shell pass and 2 tube passes but the solution is valid for any even number of tube passes.  Solution is from Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: HX_shell&tube_2
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a shell and tube heat exchanger with 2 shell passes and 4 tube passes.
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a shell and tube heat exchanger with 2 shell passes and 4 tube passes.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 2-4 TEMA E shell and tube heat exchanger has an E type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at one end and leaves at the other.  It consists of two shell passes and 4 tube passes but the solution is valid for any even number of tube passes.  Solution is from Nellis and Klein{linkID=9010}.

Routines.Name: HX_shell&tube_N
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a shell and tube heat exchanger with N shell passes and 2N tube passes.
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a shell and tube heat exchanger with N shell passes and 2N tube passes.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  An N-2N TEMA E shell and tube heat exchanger has an E type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at one end and leaves at the other.  It consists of N shell passes and 2xN tube passes.   Solution is from Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: HX_12TEMAE_2shellsidestreams
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a shell and tube heat exchanger with parallel shell-side flows.
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a shell and tube heat exchanger with parallel shell side flows.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 1-2 TEMA E shell and tube heat exchanger with parallel shell flows has an E type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at one end and leaves at the other.  However, the shell fluid is split into two parallel streams such that each stream interacts with only one tube pass.  Solution is from Rohsenow et al.

Routines.Name: HX_13TEMAE
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a 13 TEMA E Shell and Tube Heat Exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a 13 TEMA-E shell and tube heat exchanger.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 1-3 TEMA E shell and tube heat exchanger has an E type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at one end and leaves at the other.  It consists of one shell pass and 3 tube passes.  Note that the solution provided is for the more optimal case where the shell side flows are in counterflow for 2 of the 3 tube passes.  Solution is from Rohsenow et al.

Routines.Name: HX_11TEMAG
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a 11 TEMA G Shell and Tube Heat Exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a 11 TEMA-G shell and tube heat exchanger.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 1-1 TEMA G shell and tube heat exchanger has an G type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at the center, splits and flows to each end, and then turns around and leaves at the center.  The single tube pass moves from one end of the heat exchanger to the other.  Solution is from Rohsenow et al.

Routines.Name: HX_12TEMAG
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a 12 TEMA G Shell and Tube Heat Exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a 12 TEMA-G shell and tube heat exchanger.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 1-2 TEMA G shell and tube heat exchanger has an G type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at the center, splits and flows to each end, and then turns around and leaves at the center.  The two tube passes are arranged in an overall counterflow configuration and the shell and tube fluids are mixed in each pass at a cross section.  Solution is from Rohsenow et al.

Routines.Name: HX_11TEMAH
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a 11 TEMA H Shell and Tube Heat Exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a 11 TEMA-H shell and tube heat exchanger.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 1-1 TEMA H shell and tube heat exchanger has an H type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at two center inlets, splits and flows to each end and the center, and then leaves at two center outlets.  There is a single tube pass.  Solution is from Rohsenow et al.

Routines.Name: HX_12TEMAH
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a 12 TEMA H Shell and Tube Heat Exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a 12 TEMA-H shell and tube heat exchanger.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 1-2 TEMA H shell and tube heat exchanger has an H type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at two center inlets, splits and flows to each end and the center, and then leaves at two center outlets.  The two tube passes are arranged in an overall counterflow configuration and the shell and tube fluids are mixed in each pass at a cross section.  Solution is from Rohsenow et al.

Routines.Name: HX_11TEMAJ
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a 11 TEMA J Shell and Tube Heat Exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a 11 TEMA-J shell and tube heat exchanger.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 1-1 TEMA J shell and tube heat exchanger has a J type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at a center inlets, splits and flows to each end where it leaves at two outlets.  There is a single tube pass.  Solution is from Rohsenow et al.

Routines.Name: HX_12TEMAJ
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a 12 TEMA J Shell and Tube Heat Exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a 12 TEMA-J shell and tube heat exchanger.
Routines.LongDescription: A shell and tube heat exchanger consists of an outer shell filled with a tube bank.  The shell side fluid flows in the shell, around the tube, while the tube side fluid flows through the tubes.   There are many shell and tube configurations characterized by, among other things, the shell type and the number and configuration of the shell and tube flows.  A 1-2TEMA J shell and tube heat exchanger has a J type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at a center inlets, splits and flows to each end where it leaves at two outlets.  There are 2 tube passes.  Solution is from Rohsenow et al.  Note that the 1-2 TEMA J Shell and Tube heat exchanger configuration has an effectiveness that is not monotonically increasing with NTU due to the parallel- and counter-flow nature of the heat exchanger.  Therefore it is not possible to determine a unique value of NTU corresponding to an effectiveness.

Routines.Name: HX_14TEMAJ

A 1-4 TEMA J shell and tube heat exchanger has a J type shell in which the shell side fluid enters at a center inlets, splits and flows to each end where it leaves at two outlets.  There are 4 tube passes.  Solution is from Rohsenow et al. Routines.Name: HX_Regenerator
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness-NTU relation for a balanced, counterflow regenerator
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness-NTU solution for a balanced counterflow regenerator.
Routines.LongDescription: A regenerator heat exchanger is an indirect heat transfer device where a hot fluid transfers heat to a solid at one point in the process and the solid then transfers heat to a cold fluid at a different point.  A balanced regenerator is one where the hot and cold fluids have the same capacitance rate.  The effectiveness-NTU solution is available for a balanced counterflow regenerator.  A numerical model that can include unbalanced situations is available in the procedure RegeneratorHX.  Solution is from Dragutinovic and Baclic.

Routines.Name: HX_cof_crfhdr
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness of a counterflow heat exchanger that has cross-flow headers.
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness of a counterflow heat exchanger that has cross-flow headers.
Routines.LongDescription: Effectiveness of a counterflow heat exchanger that has cross-flow headers. The solution is obtained using the method suggested by Kays et al. (1968) in which a counterflow heat exchanger is placed in series with a cross-flow (both fluids unmixed) heat exchanger.

Routines.Name: AxialConductionHX
Routines.DisplayName: Effectiveness of a counterflow heat exchanger that has axial conduction.
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the effectiveness of a counterflow heat exchanger that has axial conduction.
Routines.LongDescription: AxialConductionHX provides a finite difference analysis of a counterflow heat exchanger with a consideration of axial conduction in the manner described in section 8.6.4 of Nellis and Klein.  The numerical model uses 500 nodes with an exponential spacing that concentrates nodes at the ends of the heat exchanger.  The spacing is controlled by the value of input gamma.  If the value of gamma is set to 0, the grid will be uniform. Increasing values of gamma providing more nodes at the ends of the heat exchanger.   The units of the inputs and outputs to this Subprogram must be as indicate above, regardless of the settings in the EES unit system dialog.

Routines.Name: RegeneratorHX
Routines.DisplayName: Performance of a counterflow regenerator
Routines.ShortDescription: RegeneratorHX implements a general numerical solution for a regenerator.
Routines.LongDescription: RegeneratorHX implements a general numerical solution for a regenerator. The model is described in Section 8.10.5 of Nellis and Klein. The numerical model uses 10 spatial nodes and 20 nodes in time for each blow process.

Routines.Name: LMTD_CF_parallelflow
Routines.DisplayName: Log mean temperature difference for a parallel flow heat exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the log mean temperature difference correction factor for a parallel flow heat exchanger.
Routines.LongDescription: LMTD_CF returns the correction factor needed to determine the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) of a heat exchanger with a flow configuration other than counterflow.  LMTD_CF is 1 by definition for counterflow but it will be less than one for other flow configurations as presented in Section 8.2 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.LongDescription: LMTD_CF returns the correction factor needed to determine the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) of a heat exchanger with a flow configuration other than counterflow.  LMTD_CF is 1 by definition for counterflow but it will be less than one for other flow configurations as presented in Section 8.2 of Nellis and Klein.
