Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the log mean temperature difference correction factor for a cross flow heat exchanger with one fluid mixed.
Routines.LongDescription: LMTD_CF returns the correction factor needed to determine the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) of a heat exchanger with a flow configuration other than counterflow.  LMTD_CF is 1 by definition for counterflow but it will be less than one for other flow configurations as presented in Section 8.2 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: LMTD_CF_shell&tube_1
Routines.DisplayName: Log mean temperature difference for a shell and tube heat exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the log mean temperature difference correction factor for a shell and tube heat exchanger with 1 shell pass and 2 tube passes.
Routines.LongDescription: LMTD_CF returns the correction factor needed to determine the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) of a heat exchanger with a flow configuration other than counterflow.  LMTD_CF is 1 by definition for counterflow but it will be less than one for other flow configurations as presented in Section 8.2 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: LMTD_CF_shell&tube_N
Routines.DisplayName: Log mean temperature difference for a shell and tube heat exchanger
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the log mean temperature difference correction factor for a shell and tube heat exchanger with N shell pass and 2N tube passes.
Routines.LongDescription: LMTD_CF returns the correction factor needed to determine the log mean temperature difference (LMTD) of a heat exchanger with a flow configuration other than counterflow.  LMTD_CF is 1 by definition for counterflow but it will be less than one for other flow configurations as presented in Section 8.2 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: K_Sudden_Expansion
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss coefficient for a sudden expansion
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Sudden_Expansion returns the resistance coefficient for an abrupt expansion flow process.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Sudden_Expansion returns the resistance coefficient for an abrupt expansion flow process where fluid goes from a smaller round pipe to a larger round pipe.  Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979.

Routines.Name: pipeflow_f
Routines.DisplayName: Pressure drop in a straight pipe
Routines.ShortDescription: PipeFlow_f returns the pressure drop and friction factor for flow through a straight pipe.
Routines.LongDescription: PipeFlow_f returns the pressure drop and friction factor for flow through a straight pipe.  The procedure will determine if the flow is laminar or turbulent.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynold's numbers between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations.  The ratio of L/D is used to apply a developing flow correction; set L to a large number if developing flow corrections are not applicable.

Routines.Name: ductflow_f
Routines.DisplayName: Pressure drop in a straight duct
Routines.ShortDescription: DuctFlow_f returns the pressure drop and friction factor for flow through a straight duct.
Routines.LongDescription: DuctFlow_f returns the pressure drop and friction factor for flow through a straight duct with rectangular cross section. The procedure is applicable for developing flow or fully-developed flow in the laminar, transitional or turbulent flow regimes. The procedure will determine if the flow is laminar or turbulent.  Transitional flow is assumed to occur for Reynold's numbers between 2300 and 3000 and interpolation is applied between the laminar and turbulent correlations.

Routines.Name: K_Gradual_Expansion
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss coefficient for a gradual expansion
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Gradual_Expansion returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual expansion.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Gradual_Expansion returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual expansion from a smaller pipe to a larger pipe.  For expansion angles greater than 45 deg, the resistance coefficient is the same as for a sudden expansion.  Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979.

Routines.Name: K_Gradual_Expansion2
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss coefficient for a gradual expansion
Routines.ShortDescription: K_gradual_expansion2 returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual expansion with a long discharge ducts given the ratio of the exit to inlet areas and the half angle.
Routines.LongDescription: K_gradual_expansion2 returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual expansion with a long discharge ducts given the ratio of the exit to inlet areas and the half angle.  he correlations work for either rectangular or circular ducts.  Note that the function DuctGradualExpansion_Long_CL in the component library implements the dimensional version of this function.  This function differs from K_gradual_expansion in that it uses correlations from Legg (2017) rather than Crane (1979); these tend to provide larger values of the loss coefficient.

Routines.Name: K_Grad_Exp_Circ_Free
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss coefficient for a gradual expansion
Routines.ShortDescription: K_grad_exp_circ_free returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual expansion with no discharge ducts given the ratio of the exit to inlet areas and the half angle.  The correlation is for circular ducts.
Routines.LongDescription: K_grad_exp_circ_free returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual expansion with no discharge ducts given the ratio of the exit to inlet areas and the half angle.  The correlation is for circular ducts.  Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_Grad_Exp_Rect_Free
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss coefficient for a gradual expansion
Routines.ShortDescription: K_grad_exp_rect_free returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual expansion with no discharge ducts given the ratio of the exit to inlet areas and the half angle.
Routines.LongDescription: K_grad_exp_rect_free returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual expansion with no discharge ducts given the ratio of the exit to inlet areas and the half angle.  The correlation is for rectangular ducts. Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_Sudden_Contraction
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss coefficient for a sudden contraction
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Sudden_Contraction returns the resistance coefficient for an abrupt expansion flow process.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Sudden_Contraction returns the resistance coefficient for an abrupt expansion flow process where a larger pipe connects to a smaller one. Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979 and Pipe Friction Manual, Hydraulic Institute, New York, 1962, p. 34.

Routines.Name: K_Gradual_Contraction
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss coefficient for a gradual contraction
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Gradual_Contraction returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual contraction from one tube to another.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Gradual_Contraction returns the resistance coefficient for a gradual contraction from one tube to another.  For expansion angles greater than 45 degree, the resistance coefficient is the same as for a sudden expansion.

Routines.Name: K_c_CircularTubeHeader
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for header where flow enters a set of circular tubes
Routines.ShortDescription: K_c_CircularTubeHeader returns the contraction coefficient for a header in which flow enters a set of circular tubes.
Routines.LongDescription: K_c_CircularTubeHeader returns the contraction coefficient for a header in which flow enters a set of circular tubes. For Re>3000 the solution from Kays and London (1984) are used for turbulent flow.  For Re<2000 the information presented in Webb (2006) is used.  From 2000<Re<3000 the result is interpolated between laminar and turbulent.

Routines.Name: K_e_CircularTubeHeader
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for header where flow leaves a set of circular tubes
Routines.ShortDescription: K_e_CircularTubeHeader returns the expansion coefficient for flow leaving a set of circular tubes.
Routines.LongDescription: K_e_CircularTubeHeader returns the expansion coefficient for flow leaving a set of circular tubes.  For Re>3000 the solution from Kays and London (1984) are used for turbulent flow.  For Re<2000 the information presented in Webb (2006) is used.  From 2000<Re<3000 the result is interpolated between laminar and turbulent.

Routines.Name: K_c_ParallelPlateHeader
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for header where flow enters a set of parallel plates
Routines.ShortDescription: K_c_ParallelPlateHeader returns the contraction coefficient for a header in which flow enters a set of parallel plate passages.
Routines.LongDescription: K_c_ParallelPlateHeader returns the contraction coefficient for a header in which flow enters a set of parallel plate passages.  For Re>3000 the solution from Kays and London (1984) are used for turbulent flow.  For Re<2000 the solution presented in Webb (2006) is used.  From 2000<Re<3000 the result is interpolated between laminar and turbulent.

Routines.Name: K_e_ParallelPlateHeader
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for header where flow leaves a set of parallel channels
Routines.ShortDescription: K_e_ParallelPlateHeader returns the expansion coefficient for flow leaving a set of parallel plate passages.
Routines.LongDescription: K_e_ParallelPlateHeader returns the expansion coefficient for flow leaving a set of parallel plate passages. For Re>3000 the solution from Kays and London (1984) are used for turbulent flow.  For Re<2000 the solution presented in Webb (2006) is used.  From 2000<Re<3000 the result is interpolated between laminar and turbulent.

Routines.Name: K_c_SquareChannelHeader
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for header where flow enters a set of square channels
Routines.ShortDescription: K_c_SquareChannelHeader returns the contraction coefficient for a header in which flow enters a set of square channels.
Routines.LongDescription: K_c_SquareChannelHeader returns the contraction coefficient for a header in which flow enters a set of square channels. For Re>3000 the solution from Kays and London (1984) are used for turbulent flow.  For Re<2000 the solution presented in Webb (2006) is used.  From 2000<Re<3000 the result is interpolated between laminar and turbulent.

Routines.Name: K_e_SquareChannelHeader
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for header where flow leaves a set of square channels
Routines.ShortDescription: K_e_SquareChannelHeader returns the expansion coefficient for flow leaving a set of square channels.
Routines.LongDescription: K_e_SquareChannelHeader returns the expansion coefficient for flow leaving a set of square channels. For Re>3000 the solution from Kays and London (1984) are used for turbulent flow.  For Re<2000 the solution presented in Webb (2006) is used.  From 2000<Re<3000 the result is interpolated between laminar and turbulent.

Routines.Name: K_c_TriangularChannelHeader
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for header where flow enters a set of triangular channels
Routines.ShortDescription: K_c_TriangularChannelHeader returns the contraction coefficient for a header in which flow enters a set of triangular channels.
Routines.LongDescription: K_c_TriangularChannelHeader returns the contraction coefficient for a header in which flow enters a set of triangular channels. For Re>3000 the solution from Kays and London (1984) are used for turbulent flow.  For Re<2000 the solution presented in Webb (2006) is used.  From 2000<Re<3000 the result is interpolated between laminar and turbulent.

Routines.Name: K_e_TriangularChannelHeader
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for header where flow leaves a set of triangular channels
Routines.ShortDescription: K_e_TriangularChannelHeader returns the expansion coefficient for flow leaving a set of triangular channels.
Routines.LongDescription: K_e_TriangularChannelHeader returns the expansion coefficient for flow leaving a set of triangular channels.  For Re>3000 the solution from Kays and London (1984) are used for turbulent flow.  For Re<2000 the solution presented in Webb (2006) is used.  From 2000<Re<3000 the result is interpolated between laminar and turbulent.

Routines.Name: K_Rounded_Pipe_Inlet
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a rounded entrance to a pipe
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Rounded_Pipe_Inlet returns the resistance coefficient for a rounded inlet.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Rounded_Pipe_Inlet returns the resistance coefficient for a rounded inlet.  Note that the velocity that should be used with this resistance coefficient is the velocity well beyond the inlet where the diameter is D.  Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979, page A-29.

Routines.Name: K_Sharp_Edged_Pipe_Inlet
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a sharp entrance to a pipe
Routines.ShortDescription: The resistance coefficient for a sharped-edged pipe inlet.
Routines.LongDescription: The resistance coefficient for a sharped-edged pipe inlet is 0.5.  This function requires the pipe diameter as an input, but it is not used in the determination of the resistance coefficient.  Solution is from Page A-29 of Crane, "Flow of Fluids through Valves, Fittings and pipe", Technical Paper No. 410M, Crane Co, NY, 1979.

Routines.Name: K_Reentrant_Pipe_Inlet
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a sharp reentrant inlet to a pipe
Routines.ShortDescription: The resistance coefficient for a reentrant pipe inlet.
Routines.LongDescription: The resistance coefficient for a reentrant pipe inlet is approximately 0.8 provided that t<<D and l is approximately 0.1 D.

Routines.Name: K_Rounded_Pipe_Exit
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a rounded exit to a pipe.
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Rounded_Pipe_Exit returns the resistance coefficient for a rounded exit for laminar or turbulent flow.
Routines.LongDescription: The resistance coefficient is nearly independent of the radius of curvature and so it has the same value as the sharp-edged exit.  Solution is from Cengel and Cimbala, Fluid Mechanics, Fundamentals and Applications,McGraw-Hill, 2006.

Routines.Name: K_Sharp_Edged_Pipe_Exit
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a sharp edged exit to a pipe.
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Sharp_edged_Pipe_Exit returns the resistance coefficient for a sharp-edged exit.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Sharp_edged_Pipe_Exit returns the resistance coefficient for a sharp-edged exit. Solution is from Cengel and Cimbala, Fluid Mechanics, Fundamentals and Applications,McGraw-Hill, 2006.

Routines.Name: K_Reentrant_Pipe_Exit
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for the exit from a reentrant pipe
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Reentrant_Pipe_Exit returns the resistance coefficient for reentrant exit.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Reentrant_Pipe_Exit returns the resistance coefficient for reentrant exit. Solution is from Cengel and Cimbala, Fluid Mechanics, Fundamentals and Applications,McGraw-Hill, 2006.

Routines.Name: K_90deg_bend
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a 90 degree bend
Routines.ShortDescription: K_90deg_bend function returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree bend.
Routines.LongDescription: K_90deg_bend function returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree bend.  The relative roughness must also be supplied as a parameter.  This parameter should be set to 0 for smooth tubes and it should be less than 0.002 for this function.  The resistance factor is applicable to turbulent flow.  Solution is from Pipe Friction Manual, Hydraulic Institute, New York, 1962.

Routines.Name: K_bend
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a bend of arbitrary angle
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Bend returns the resistance coefficient for a bend given its bend radius to diameter ratio and the turning angle.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Bend returns the resistance coefficient for a bend given its bend radius to diameter ratio and the turning angle.  Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_bend_rect
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a bend in a rectangular duct
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Bend_rect returns the resistance coefficient for a rectangular duct bend.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Bend_rect returns the resistance coefficient for a rectangular duct bend.  Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_miterbend
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a miter bend in a rectangular duct
Routines.ShortDescription: K_miterbend(alpha, RelRough) function returns the resistance coefficient for a miter bend.
Routines.LongDescription: K_miterbend(alpha, RelRough) function returns the resistance coefficient for a miter bend.  The relative roughness must also be supplied as a parameter, ranging between 0 for smooth surfaces to 0.05 for very rough surfaces.  Solution is from Pipe Friction Manual, Hydraulic Institute, New York, 1962.

Routines.Name: K_90deg_elbow
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a 90 degree elbow
Routines.ShortDescription: K_90deg_elbow function returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree elbow.
Routines.LongDescription: K_90deg_elbow function returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree elbow.  The relative roughness must also be supplied as a parameter.  This parameter can range between 0 (for smooth tubes) to 0.05 (for very rough tubes).   Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979, p A-29.

Routines.Name: K_45deg_elbow
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a 45 degree elbow
Routines.ShortDescription: K_45deg_elbow returns the resistance coefficient for a 45 degree elbow.
Routines.LongDescription: K_45deg_elbow returns the resistance coefficient for a 45 degree elbow. The relative roughness must also be supplied as a parameter.  This parameter can range between 0 (for smooth tubes) to 0.05 (for very rough tubes).   Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979, p A-29.

Routines.Name: K_ReturnBend
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a return bend
Routines.ShortDescription: K_Returnbend returns the resistance coefficient for a return bend.
Routines.LongDescription: K_Returnbend returns the resistance coefficient for a return bend.   The relative roughness must also be supplied as a parameter.  This parameter can range between 0 (for smooth tubes) to 0.05 (for very rough tubes).   Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979, p A-29.

Routines.Name: K_supply_branch_90
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a supply branch at 90 degree
Routines.ShortDescription: K_supply_branch_90 returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree supply branch.
Routines.LongDescription: K_supply_branch_90 returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree supply branch.  The coefficient returned is for the branch and should be applied to the upstream main duct velocity.  The coefficient is a function of the ratio of the branch to upstream volumetric flow rates and the ratio of the branch to upstream areas.  The correlation is for circular ducts.  Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_supply_branch_conical_90
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a supply branch at 90 degree with a conical inlet
Routines.ShortDescription: K_supply_branch_conical_90 returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree supply branch with a conical inlet.
Routines.LongDescription: K_supply_branch_conical_90 returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree supply branch with a conical inlet. The coefficient returned is for the branch and should be applied to the upstream main duct velocity.  The coefficient is a function of the ratio of the branch to upstream volumetric flow rates and the ratio of the branch to upstream  areas.  The correlation is for circular ducts.  Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_supply_branch_45
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a supply branch at 45 degree
Routines.ShortDescription: K_supply_branch_45 returns the resistance coefficient for a 45 degree supply branch.
Routines.LongDescription: K_supply_branch_45 returns the resistance coefficient for a 45 degree supply branch.  The coefficient returned is for the branch and should be applied to the upstream main duct velocity.  Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_supply_main
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for the main duct with a supply branch
Routines.ShortDescription: K_supply_main returns the resistance coefficient for a supply duct.
Routines.LongDescription: K_supply_main returns the resistance coefficient for a supply duct.  The coefficient returned is for the main duct and should be applied to the upstream main duct velocity.  The correlation is for circular ducts. Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_supply_tee
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a supply duct with two T ducts
Routines.ShortDescription: K_supply_tee returns the resistance coefficient for a supply duct with two tee ducts of equal area.
Routines.LongDescription: K_supply_tee returns the resistance coefficient for a supply duct with two tee ducts of equal area.  The coefficient returned is for the duct 1 and should be applied to the upstream main duct velocity.  The correlation is for circular ducts. Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_extract_branch_45
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for an extract branch at 45 degree
Routines.ShortDescription: K_extract_branch_45 returns the resistance coefficient for a 45 degree extract branch.
Routines.LongDescription: K_extract_branch_45 returns the resistance coefficient for a 45 degree extract branch.  The coefficient returned is for the branch and should be applied to the downstream main duct velocity.  The correlation is for circular ducts.

Routines.Name: K_extract_main_45
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for the main duct with an extract branch at 45 degree
Routines.ShortDescription: K_extract_main_45 returns the resistance coefficient for a 45 degree extract branch.
Routines.LongDescription: K_extract_main_45 returns the resistance coefficient for a 45 degree extract branch.  The coefficient returned is for the main flow and should be applied to the downstream main duct velocity.  The correlation is for circular ducts. Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_extract_branch_90
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for an extract branch at 90 degree
Routines.ShortDescription: K_extract_branch_90 returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree extract branch.
Routines.LongDescription: K_extract_branch_90 returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree extract branch.  The coefficient returned is for the branch and should be applied to the downstream main duct velocity.  The correlation is for circular ducts.  Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_extract_main_90
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for the main duct with an extract branch at 90 degree
Routines.ShortDescription: K_extract_main_90 returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree extract branch.
Routines.LongDescription: K_extract_main_90 returns the resistance coefficient for a 90 degree extract branch.  The coefficient returned is for the main flow and should be applied to the downstream main duct velocity.  The correlation is for circular ducts.  Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_extract_tee
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for an extraction branch with two Ts
Routines.ShortDescription: K_extract_tee returns the resistance coefficient for an extract duct with two tee ducts of equal area.
Routines.LongDescription: K_extract_tee returns the resistance coefficient for an extract duct with two tee ducts of equal area. The coefficient returned is for the duct 1 and should be applied to the downstream duct velocity.  The correlation is for circular ducts.  Solution is from Legg, R., 2017, "Chapter 14: Ducted Air Systems" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_AngleValve
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for an angle valve
Routines.ShortDescription: K_AngleValve returns the resistance coefficient for a fully-open or partially open angle valve.
Routines.LongDescription: K_AngleValve returns the resistance coefficient for a fully-open or partially open angle valve.  Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979.

Routines.Name: K_GateValve
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a gate valve
Routines.ShortDescription: K_GateValve returns the resistance coefficient for a fully-open or partially open non-tapered gate valve.
Routines.LongDescription: K_GateValve returns the resistance coefficient for a fully-open or partially open non-tapered gate valve.  Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979 and Churchill, S.W. 1977, 'Friction Factor Spans All Fluid Flow Regimes,' Chem. Eng. (Rugby, U.K.) 84(24), pp.91-91).

Routines.Name: K_GlobeValve
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a globe valve
Routines.ShortDescription: K_GlobeValve returns the resistance coefficient for a fully-open or partially globe valve.
Routines.LongDescription: K_GlobeValve returns the resistance coefficient for a fully-open or partially globe valve.  Solution from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979.

Routines.Name: K_SwingCheckValve
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a swing check valve
Routines.ShortDescription: K_SwingCheckValve returns the resistance coefficient for a swing check valve.
Routines.LongDescription: K_SwingCheckValve returns the resistance coefficient for a swing check valve.  Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979.

Routines.Name: K_Damper_Parallel
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a damper with parallel vanes
Routines.ShortDescription: K_damper_parallel returns the resistance coefficient for a damper with parallel vanes.
Routines.LongDescription: K_damper_parallel returns the resistance coefficient for a damper with parallel vanes.

Routines.Name: K_Damper_Opposed
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a damper with opposed vanes
Routines.ShortDescription: K_damper_opposed returns the resistance coefficient for a damper with opposed vanes.
Routines.LongDescription: K_damper_opposed returns the resistance coefficient for a damper with opposed vanes.  Solution is from Dwyer, T., 2017, "Chapter 17: Controls, Dampers, and Valves" in Air Conditioning System Design, Butterworth-Heinemann.

Routines.Name: K_Tee_Straight
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a T joint
Routines.ShortDescription: K_tee_straight returns the resistance coefficient for standard T with flow straight through (i.e., not through the branch).
Routines.LongDescription: K_tee_straight returns the resistance coefficient for standard T with flow straight through (i.e., not through the branch).  Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979, p A-29.

Routines.Name: K_Tee_branched
Routines.DisplayName: Minor loss for a T joint
Routines.ShortDescription: K_tee_branched returns the resistance coefficient for standard T with flow primarily through the branch.
Routines.LongDescription: K_tee_branched returns the resistance coefficient for standard T with flow primarily through the branch.  Solution is from Flow of Fluids Through Valves, Fittings, and Pipe, Crane Valves North America, Technical Paper No. 410M. 1979, p A-29.

Routines.Name: OrificePlate
Routines.DisplayName: Pressure drop for an orifice plate
Routines.ShortDescription: The OrificePlate procedure returns the pressure drop across a stand orifice plate for steady, incompressible, horizontal flow.
Routines.LongDescription: The OrificePlate procedure returns the pressure drop across a stand orifice plate for steady, incompressible, horizontal flow.  Solution is from Cengel, and Cimbala, Fluid Mechanics, Fundamentals and Applications, 3rd edition, McGraw-Hill, 2014, Chapter 8, Section 8.

Routines.Name: FlowNozzle
Routines.DisplayName: Pressure drop for a flow nozzle
Routines.ShortDescription: The FlowNozzle procedure returns the pressure drop across a flow nozzle for steady, incompressible, horizontal flow.
Routines.LongDescription: The FlowNozzle procedure returns the pressure drop across a flow nozzle for steady, incompressible, horizontal flow.

Routines.Name: Emittance_CO2_H2O
Routines.DisplayName: Emissivity of a gas volume
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides the emissivity of a mixture of CO2, H2O and other, non-participating gases.
Routines.LongDescription: Provides the emissivity of a mixture of CO2, H2O and other, non-participating gases.

Routines.Name: F2D_1
Routines.DisplayName: Infinitely long directly opposed parallel plates
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinitely long directly opposed parallel plates.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinitely long directly opposed parallel plates. Function f2d_1(h, w) returns the view factor between two infinitely long, directly opposed parallel plates of the same finite width. Reference: Siegel and Howell, Thermal radiation heat transfer , 4th edition, p.843.

Routines.Name: F2D_2
Routines.DisplayName: Infinitely long plates at angle alpha
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinitely long plates at angle alpha.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinitely long plates at angle alpha. Function f2d_2(alpha, w) returns the view factor between two infinitely long plates of the same finite width having a common edge and having an included angle a to each other. Reference: Siegel and Howell, Thermal radiation heat transfer , 4th edition, p.844.

Routines.Name: F2D_3
Routines.DisplayName: Infinite cylinder to unsymmetric finite width plate
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinite cylinder to unsymmetric finite width plate.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinite cylinder to unsymmetric finite width plate. Function f2d_3(r, a, b_1, b_2) calculates the view factor from an an infinitely long cylinder to an unsymmetrically placed plate of finite width. Reference: http://www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-62.html

Routines.Name: F2D_4
Routines.DisplayName: Infinite cylinder to cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinite cylinder to cylinder.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinite cylinder to cylinder. Function f2d_4(r, s) provides the view factor from an infinitely long cylinder to a parallel infinitely long cylinder of identical diameter. Reference: Siegel and Howell, Thermal radiation heat transfer , 4th edition, p.847.

Routines.Name: F2D_5
Routines.DisplayName: Infinite concentric cylinders
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinite concentric cylinders.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinite concentric cylinders. Function f2d_5(r_1, r_2) provides the view factor between two infinitely long concentric cylinders. Reference: Siegel and Howell, Thermal radiation heat transfer , 4th edition, p.847.

Routines.Name: F2D_6
Routines.DisplayName: Infinite cylinder to symmetric finite width plate
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinite cylinder to symmetric finite width plate.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinite cylinder to symmetric finite width plate. Function f2d_6(a,b) returns the view factor from an infinitely long cylinder a symmetrically placed finite width plate of infinite length. Notes: The cylinder radius must be less than the perpendicular distance, a, from the cylinder axis to the plate. Reference: Howell, Radiation Configuration Factors, www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-61.html .

Routines.Name: F2D_7
Routines.DisplayName: Infinite plane to row of cylinders
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinite plane to row of cylinders.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinite plane to row of cylinders. Function f2d_7(d,s) returns the view factor from an infinite plane to a row of infinite cylinders that parallel to each other. Reference: Incropera, F. & Dewitt, D. Fundamentals of heat and mass transfer , 5th edition. John Wiley and Sons, 2002. p. 794.

Routines.Name: F2D_8
Routines.DisplayName: Semicircular tube to itself with cylinder interposed
Routines.ShortDescription: Semicircular tube to itself with cylinder interposed.
Routines.LongDescription: Semicircular tube to itself with cylinder interposed. Function f2d_8(r1, r2) returns the view factor from an infinite semicircle to itself while an infinite cylinder is positioned at the center of the semicircle. Reference: Howell, J. A catalog of radiation configuration factors . New York: McGraw Hill, 1982. p. 145.

Routines.Name: F2D_9
Routines.DisplayName: Infinite cylinder to cylinder of different radius
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinite cylinder to cylinder of different radius.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinite cylinder to cylinder of different radius. Function f2d_9(r_1,r_2,s) returns the view factor from an infinitely long cylinder of radius r_1 to a parallel infinitely long cylinder of radius r_2. Reference: Incropera, F. & Dewitt, D. Fundamentals of heat and mass transfer , 5th edition. John Wiley and Sons, 2002. p. 794.

Routines.Name: F2D_10
Routines.DisplayName: Infinite Parallel Plates of Differing Widths with Common Centerline
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinite Parallel Plates of Differing Widths with Common Centerline.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinite Parallel Plates of Differing Widths with Common Centerline. Function f2d_10(a, b, c) returns the view factor between two infinitely long, directly opposed parallel plates that can have different widths. Reference: Rohsenow W.M., et al., Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3rd ed, McGraw-Hill, p. 7.80.

Routines.Name: F2D_11
Routines.DisplayName: Infinitely long enclosure formed by three planar or convex surfaces
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinitely long enclosure formed by three planar or convex surfaces.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinitely long enclosure formed by three planar or convex surfaces. Function f2d_11(A1, A2, A3) returns the view factor from on planar or convex surface to a second planar on convex surface in an enclosure that extends to infinity in the direction into the screen. Reference: Rohsenow W.M., et al., Handbook of Heat Transfer , 3rd ed, McGraw-Hill, p. 7.80.

Routines.Name: F2D_12
Routines.DisplayName: Two infinitely long perpendicular plates of unequal widths having one common edge
Routines.ShortDescription: Two infinitely long perpendicular plates of unequal widths having one common edge.
Routines.LongDescription: Two infinitely long perpendicular plates of unequal widths having one common edge. Reference: http://www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-3.html

Routines.Name: F2D_13
Routines.DisplayName: Two infinitely long plates of unequal width having a common edge with an included angle
Routines.ShortDescription: Two infinitely long plates of unequal width having a common edge with an included angle.
Routines.LongDescription: Two infinitely long plates of unequal width having a common edge with an included angle. Reference: http://www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-5.html

Routines.Name: F2D_14
Routines.DisplayName: Infinite plate to parallel infinite plate
Routines.ShortDescription: Infinite plate to parallel infinite plate.
Routines.LongDescription: Infinite plate to parallel infinite plate. Function f2d_14 returns the view factor an infinitely long flat plate to another, parallel infinitely long flat plate. The calling protocol is: F=f2d_14(W1, W2, H, a). Reference: http://www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-2a.html

Routines.Name: F2D_15
Routines.DisplayName: Two infinitely long plates without a common edge angled with respect to one another
Routines.ShortDescription: Two infinitely long plates without a common edge angled with respect to one another.
Routines.LongDescription: Two infinitely long plates without a common edge angled with respect to one another. Function f2d_15 returns the view factor from an infinitely long flat plate to another infinitely long plate. The plates do not have to share a common edge. The included angle between them is a . The calling protocol is: F= f2d_15(x1, x2, y1, y2, alpha). Reference: http://www.thermalradiation.net/calc/sectionc/C-5.html

Routines.Name: F2D_16
Routines.DisplayName: An infinite surface to an in-line array of infinitely long tubes with n rows
Routines.ShortDescription: An infinite surface to an in-line array of infinitely long tubes with n rows.
Routines.LongDescription: An infinite surface to an in-line array of infinitely long tubes with n rows. Function f2d_16 returns the view factor from an infinitely long flat plate to an in-line array of infinitely long tubes composed of n rows. The calling protocol is: F = f2d_16(d, s, n). Reference: http://www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-7.html

Routines.Name: F2D_17
Routines.DisplayName: An infinite surface to the second row of an equilateral triangle array of infinitely long tubes
Routines.ShortDescription: An infinite surface to the second row of an equilateral triangle array of infinitely long tubes.
Routines.LongDescription: An infinite surface to the second row of an equilateral triangle array of infinitely long tubes. Function f2d_17 returns the view factor from an infinitely long flat plate to the second row of an equilateral triangle array of tubes. The calling protocol is: F = f2d_17(d, p). Reference: http://www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-8.html

Routines.Name: F3D_Poly
Routines.DisplayName: Polygon to polygon
Routines.ShortDescription: Polygon to polygon.
Routines.LongDescription: Polygon to polygon. Procedure f3d_poly(NA,NB,xA[1..NA],yA[1..NA],zA[1..NA],xB[1..NB],yB[1..NB],zB[1..NB]:F_AB,F_BA,areaA,areaB) The F3D_poly procedure returns the view factors between two polygons as well as their areas provided the following conditions are met: 1) polygons are planar (all vertices lie in the same plane) 2) polygons are simple (no self-intersecting polygons) 3) polygons are convex (in theory, concave polygons should work, but this remains untested) Author: Jacob Kerkhoff, University of Wisconsin-Madison, Solar Energy Laboratory Analytical solution derivation: Narayanaswamy, Arvind. "An analytic expression for radiation view factor between two arbitrarily oriented planar polygons." International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer 91 (2015): 841-847.

Routines.Name: F3D_1
Routines.DisplayName: Finite parallel plates
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite parallel plates.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite parallel plates. Function f3d_1(a, b, c) returns the view factor between two identical opposite rectangular plates. Reference: Siegel and Howell, Thermal radiation heat transfer , 4th edition, p.843.

Routines.Name: F3D_2
Routines.DisplayName: Finite perpendicular plates
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite perpendicular plates.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite perpendicular plates. Function f3d_2(a, b, c) returns the view factor from area 1 to area 2 of two finite rectangles of the same length, having one common edge and having an angle of 90 degrees to each other. Notes: The input values have to be greater than 0! Reference: Siegel and Howell, Thermal radiation heat transfer , 4th edition, p.844.

Routines.Name: F3D_3
Routines.DisplayName: Disk to disk (same center)
Routines.ShortDescription: Disk to disk (same center).
Routines.LongDescription: Disk to disk (same center). Function f3d_3(r_1, r_2, a) returns the view factor value of one disk (finite area) from another one (finite area) parallel to it which has its center along the same normal. Reference: Siegel and Howell, Thermal radiation heat transfer , 4th edition, p.845.

Routines.Name: F3D_4
Routines.DisplayName: Concentric cylinders (F_12)
Routines.ShortDescription: Concentric cylinders (F_12).
Routines.LongDescription: Concentric cylinders (F_12). Function f3d_4(r_1, r_2, w) calculates a radiation view factor between two concentric cylinders of the same finite length. f3d_4 is the view factor from the smaller of two concentric cylinders (1) to the larger cylinder (2). Reference: Siegel and Howell, Thermal radiation heat transfer , 4th edition, p.847.

Routines.Name: F3D_5
Routines.DisplayName: Concentric cylinders (F_22)
Routines.ShortDescription: Concentric cylinders (F_22).
Routines.LongDescription: Concentric cylinders (F_22). Reference: http://www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionb/C-91.html

Routines.Name: F3D_6
Routines.DisplayName: Finite cylinder to annular disk
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite cylinder to annular disk.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite cylinder to annular disk. Function f3d_6(r_1,r_2,l) returns the view factor from the exterior of a right cylinder to an annular disk at the end of the cylinder. Reference: Rea, S. Rapid method for determining concentric cylinder radiation view factors. AIAA J. , vol. 13, no. 8, pp. 1122-1123, 1975. in Howell, J. A catalog of radiation configuration factors. New York: McGraw Hill, 1982. p. 161.

Routines.Name: F3D_7
Routines.DisplayName: Sphere to finite plane
Routines.ShortDescription: Sphere to finite plane.
Routines.LongDescription: Sphere to finite plane. Function f3d_7(l1,l2, d, r) returns the view factor between a sphere of arbitrary radius to a rectangle. The normal of one of the rectangle corners passes through the centerpoint of the sphere. Although the radius of the sphere does not change the view factor, it must be smaller than the distance between the plane normal and the centerpoint; the sphere cannot intersect with the plane. Reference: Tripp, W., Hwang, C., & Crank, R. Radiation shape factors for plane surfaces and spheres, circles or cylinders, Spec. Rept. 16, Kansas State University Bulletin, vol. 46, no. 4, 1962. in Howell, J. A catalog of radiation configuration factors. New York: McGraw Hill, 1982. p. 190.

Routines.Name: F3D_8
Routines.DisplayName: Sphere to interior cylindrical surface (sphere exterior)
Routines.ShortDescription: Sphere to interior cylindrical surface (sphere exterior).
Routines.LongDescription: Sphere to interior cylindrical surface (sphere exterior). Function f3d_8(r1,r2,a1,a2) returns the view factor between a sphere and the interior of a cylindrical surface (cylinder without ends). The centerpoint of the sphere falls along the axis of the cylindrical surface, and the sphere must be completely outside the cylinder. The radius of the sphere must be smaller than that of the cylinder. Reference: Feingold, A, & Gupta, K. New analytical approach to the evaluation of configuration factors in radiation from spheres and infinitely long cylinders. ASME J. Heat Transfer , vol. 92, no. 1, pp 69-76. in Howell, J. A catalog of radiation configuration factors. New York: McGraw Hill, 1982. p. 197.

Routines.Name: F3D_9
Routines.DisplayName: Sphere to interior cylindrical surface (sphere interior)
Routines.ShortDescription: Sphere to interior cylindrical surface (sphere interior).
Routines.LongDescription: Sphere to interior cylindrical surface (sphere interior). Function f3d_9(r1,r2,a) returns the view factor between a sphere and the interior of a cylindrical surface (cylinder without ends). The centerpoint of the sphere falls along the axis of the cylindrical surface, and the sphere must be completely inside the cylinder. The radius of the sphere must be smaller than that of the cylinder. Reference: Feingold, A, & Gupta, K. New analytical approach to the evaluation of configuration factors in radiation from spheres and infinitely long cylinders. ASME J. Heat Transfer , vol. 92, no. 1, pp 69-76. in Howell, J. A catalog of radiation configuration factors. New York: McGraw Hill, 1982. p. 197.

Routines.Name: F3D_10
Routines.DisplayName: Perpendicular rectangles
Routines.ShortDescription: Perpendicular rectangles.
Routines.LongDescription: Perpendicular rectangles. Function f3d_10(a, b1, b2,c) returns the view factor from area 1 to area 2 of two finite rectangles that are oriented perpendicular to each other as shown . Notes: The input values must all be greater than 0! Reference: Chapman A.J., Fundamentals of H eat Transfer, Macmillan Publishing Co., 1987, p. 734

Routines.Name: F3D_11
Routines.DisplayName: Perpendicular rectangles
Routines.ShortDescription: Perpendicular rectangles.
Routines.LongDescription: Perpendicular rectangles. Function f3d_11(a_1, a_2,b_1,b_2,c) returns the view factor from area 1 to area 2 of two finite rectangles that are oriented perpendicular to each other as shown . Notes: The input values must all be greater than 0! Reference: Chapman A.J., Fundamentals of H eat Transfer, Macmillan Publishing Co., 1987, p. 734

Routines.Name: F3D_12
Routines.DisplayName: Perpendicular rectangles
Routines.ShortDescription: Perpendicular rectangles.
Routines.LongDescription: Perpendicular rectangles. Function f3d_12(a, b, c1, c2) returns the view factor from area 1 to area 2 of two finite rectangles that are oriented perpendicular to each other and having one common point . Notes: The input values must all be greater than 0! Reference: Chapman A.J., Fundamentals of H eat Transfer, Macmillan Publishing Co., 1987, p. 736

Routines.Name: F3D_13
Routines.DisplayName: Perpendicular rectangles
Routines.ShortDescription: Perpendicular rectangles.
Routines.LongDescription: Perpendicular rectangles. Function f3d_13(a1, a2, b1, b2, c1, c2, c3) returns the view factor from area 1 to area 2 of two finite rectangles that are oriented perpendicular to each other and having no common points. Notes: The input values must all be greater than 0! Reference: Chapman A.J., Fundamentals of Heat Transfer, Macmillan Publishing Co., 1987, p. 738 See also: f3d_30

Routines.Name: F3D_14
Routines.DisplayName: Parallel rectangles
Routines.ShortDescription: Parallel rectangles.
Routines.LongDescription: Parallel rectangles. Function f3d_14(x1,x2,y1,y2,a1,a2,b1,b2,z) returns the view factor from area 1 to area 2 of two arbitrarily-located finite rectangles that are oriented perpendicular to each other. Notes: The input values must all be greater than 0! Reference: Howell, http://www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-13.html

Routines.Name: F3D_15
Routines.DisplayName: Finite plate to finite cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite plate to finite cylinder.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite plate to finite cylinder. Function f3d_15(l, n, z, d) returns the view factor from a finite plane to a finite cylinder. The plane and cylinder are the same height and plane edge nearest the cylinder is defined by its normal passing through the axis of the cylinder. Reference: Wiebelt, J. A. & Ruo, S. Y. Radiant-interchange configuration factors for finite right circular cylinder to rectangular planes, Int. J. Heat Mass Transfer , vol. 6, no. 2, pp. 143-146, 1963 in Howell, J. A catalog of radiation configuration factors. New York: McGraw Hill, 1982. p. 154.

Routines.Name: F3D_16
Routines.DisplayName: Sphere to disk
Routines.ShortDescription: Sphere to disk.
Routines.LongDescription: Sphere to disk. Function f3d_16(r, h) returns the view factor between a sphere (surface 1) located on a line that is normal to the center of a disk (surface 2). Reference: Rohsenow W.M., et al., Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3rd ed, McGraw-Hill, p. 7.84.

Routines.Name: F3D_17
Routines.DisplayName: Base of cylinder to inner surface
Routines.ShortDescription: Base of cylinder to inner surface.
Routines.LongDescription: Base of cylinder to inner surface. Function f3d_17(r, h) returns the view factor between the base of a right circular cylinder (surface 1) to the inside surface of a cylinder (surface 2). Reference: Rohsenow W.M., et al., Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3rd ed, McGraw-Hill, p. 7.84.

Routines.Name: F3D_18
Routines.DisplayName: Inner surface of cylinder to itself
Routines.ShortDescription: Inner surface of cylinder to itself.
Routines.LongDescription: Inner surface of cylinder to itself. Function f3d_18(r, h) returns the view factor between the inner surface of a right circular cylinder (surface 1) and itself. Reference: Rohsenow W.M., et al., Handbook of Heat Transfer, 3rd ed, McGraw-Hill, p. 7.84.

Routines.Name: F3D_19
Routines.DisplayName: Annular ring on base of cylinder to inner surface
Routines.ShortDescription: Annular ring on base of cylinder to inner surface.
Routines.LongDescription: Annular ring on base of cylinder to inner surface. Function f3d_19(r_1, r_2, h) returns the view factor between an annular right at the base (or top) of a right circular cylinder (surface 1) to the inside surface of a cylinder (surface 2). Reference: www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-83.html.

Routines.Name: F3D_20
Routines.DisplayName: Finite parallel squares
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite parallel squares.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite parallel squares.

Routines.Name: F3D_21
Routines.DisplayName: Rectangle to circular disk with same center
Routines.ShortDescription: Rectangle to circular disk with same center.
Routines.LongDescription: Rectangle to circular disk with same center. Function f3d_21(a, b, c, r, N) returns the view factor between a rectangle to a circular disk in disk that is in a plane parallel to the rectangle. The view factor is calculated using the Monte-Carlo method:. Notes: Function f3d_21 calls an external procedure named RecttoDisk.FDL which was written in FORTRAN. The FORTRAN program is able to provide the result much more quickly than an EES function.

Routines.Name: F3D_22
Routines.DisplayName: Small sphere to large sphere
Routines.ShortDescription: Small sphere to large sphere.
Routines.LongDescription: Small sphere to large sphere. Function f3d_22(r_1,r_2,s) returns the view factor between a smaller sphere to a larger sphere.

Routines.Name: F3D_23
Routines.DisplayName: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder.
Routines.LongDescription: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder. Reference: www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-98.html

Routines.Name: F3D_24
Routines.DisplayName: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder - extended
Routines.ShortDescription: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder - extended.
Routines.LongDescription: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder - extended. Function f3d_24(x,y,z,r1,r2) returns the view factor between the outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder when the small cylinder is extends beyond the large cylinder on both ends. Reference: www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-97.html

Routines.Name: F3D_25
Routines.DisplayName: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder-offset
Routines.ShortDescription: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder-offset.
Routines.LongDescription: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder-offset. Function f3d_25(x,y,l,r1,r2) returns the view factor between the outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder when the small cylinder extends beyond the large cylinder on one end. Reference: www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-96.html

Routines.Name: F3D_26
Routines.DisplayName: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder-inside
Routines.ShortDescription: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder-inside.
Routines.LongDescription: Outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder-inside. Function f3d_26(x,l,z,r1,r2) returns the view factor between the outer surface of a small cylinder to the inner surface of a large cylinder when the small cylinder is completely within the large cylinder. Reference: www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-95.html

Routines.Name: F3D_27
Routines.DisplayName: Upper surface of a finite rectangle tilted relative to an infinite plane
Routines.ShortDescription: Upper surface of a finite rectangle tilted relative to an infinite plane.
Routines.LongDescription: Upper surface of a finite rectangle tilted relative to an infinite plane. Reference: www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/C-9.html

Routines.Name: F3D_28
Routines.DisplayName: Finite adjacent plates
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite adjacent plates.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite adjacent plates. Function f3d_28(a, b, c, theta) returns the view factor from area 1 to area 2 of two finite rectangles of the same length, having one common edge with an angle theta between the plates. Notes: The input values have to be greater than 0! Reference: http://www.me.utexas.edu/~howell/sectionc/phi45.html

Routines.Name: F3D_29
Routines.DisplayName: Finite plates in separate planes
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite plates in separate planes.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite plates in separate planes. Function f3d_29(a_1, a_2,b_1,b_2,c, theta) returns the view factor from area 1 to area 2 of two finite rectangles that are oriented at an angle theata to each other as shown . Notes: The input values must all be greater than 0!

Routines.Name: F3D_30
Routines.DisplayName: Finite plates in separate planes
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite plates in separate planes.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite plates in separate planes. Function f3d_30(x_1, x_2, y_1, y_2, eta_1, eta_2, z_1, z_2, theta) returns the view factor from area 1 to area 2 of two finite non-adjacent rectangles that are oriented at an angle theta to each other as shown .

Routines.Name: F3D_31
Routines.DisplayName: Finite plate to finite smaller cylinder
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite plate to finite smaller cylinder.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite plate to finite smaller cylinder. Function f3d_31(w,h,d,k,s,N) returns the view factor from a rectangular plane (surface 1) to a finite cylinder (surface 2) that is parallel to the rectangle but shorter than the length of the rectangle. Surface 2 includes the entire cylinder area, including the ends. Notes: This routine is similar to f3d_15 which provides the same information for a cylinder that is the same length as the rectangle. This routine uses a Monte Carlo technique to calculate the view factor. The view factor algorithm was contributed by Jacob Brenner.

Routines.Name: F3D_32
Routines.DisplayName: Finite plate to finite plate with cylinder in between
Routines.ShortDescription: Finite plate to finite plate with cylinder in between.
Routines.LongDescription: Finite plate to finite plate with cylinder in between. Function returns the view factor between two equal sized rectangular surfaces with a circular cylinder placed between them. The circular cylinder must be of equal or lesser length (y-direction) than the flat plates and centered in both the x- and y-direction. Notes: This routine uses a Monte Carlo technique to calculate the view factor. The view factor algorithm was contributed by Jacob Brenner.

Routines.Name: F3D_33
Routines.DisplayName: Rectangle to perpendicular, centered disk
Routines.ShortDescription: Rectangle to perpendicular, centered disk.
Routines.LongDescription: Rectangle to perpendicular, centered disk. Function f3d_33(R, B, L) returns the view factor from a rectangle to a disk that is perpendicular to the rectangle. The plane containing the disk must include one edge of the rectangle and the disk must be touching the midpoint of that edge. Reference: Abishek, S., Srinivasa Ramanujam, K. and Katte, S.S., 1995, "View Factors between Disk/Rectangle and Rectangle in Parallel and Perpendicular Planes," J . Thermophysics , vol. 21, no. 1, pp. 236-239.

Routines.Name: F3D_34
Routines.DisplayName: Interiors of aligned rectangular enclosures
Routines.ShortDescription: Interiors of aligned rectangular enclosures.
Routines.LongDescription: Interiors of aligned rectangular enclosures. Function f3d_34(x_1, x_2, s, b, d) returns the view factor from the internal surface of two aligned rectangular enclosures. Reference: Stevenson, J.A. and Grafton, J.C., 1961, "Radiation heat transfer analysis for space vehicles," Rept. SID-61-91, North American Aviation (AFASD TR 61-119, pt. 1), Sept. 9.

Routines.Name: F3D_35
Routines.DisplayName: Parallel cylinders of finite and equal lengths
Routines.ShortDescription: Parallel cylinders of finite and equal lengths.
Routines.LongDescription: Parallel cylinders of finite and equal lengths. Function f3d_35(r_1, r_2, L, s) returns the view factor between two aligned cylinders of finite but equal length. Reference: Juul, N.H., "View Factors in Radiation Between Two Parallel Oriented Cylinders of Finite Lengths," Journal of Heat Transfer , Vol. 104, pp. 384-388, (1982).

Routines.Name: F3D_36
Routines.DisplayName: Perpendicular right triangles with coincident base
Routines.ShortDescription: Perpendicular right triangles with coincident base.
Routines.LongDescription: Perpendicular right triangles with coincident base. Function f3d_36(W,L,D) returns the view factor between two right triangles that are perpendicular to one another and share a base. Reference: Sauer, H.J., "Configuration factors for radiant energy interchange with triangular areas," ASHRAE Transactions , Vol. 80, Part 2, (1974).

Routines.Name: F3D_37
Routines.DisplayName: Right triangle to perpendicular rectangle with coincident base
Routines.ShortDescription: Right triangle to perpendicular rectangle with coincident base.
Routines.LongDescription: Right triangle to perpendicular rectangle with coincident base. Function f3d_37(W,L,D) returns the view factor between a right triangle and a perpendicular rectangle that share a base. Reference: Sauer, H.J., "Configuration factors for radiant energy interchange with triangular areas," ASHRAE Transactions , Vol. 80, Part 2, (1974).

Routines.Name: F3D_38
Routines.DisplayName: Right triangle to perpendicular right triangle sharing the same base but oriented oppositely
Routines.ShortDescription: Right triangle to perpendicular right triangle sharing the same base but oriented oppositely.
Routines.LongDescription: Right triangle to perpendicular right triangle sharing the same base but oriented oppositely. Function f3d_38(W,L,D) returns the view factor between a right triangle and a perpendicular right triangle sharing the same base but with the height on the opposite side. Reference: Sauer, H.J., "Configuration factors for radiant energy interchange with triangular areas," ASHRAE Transactions , Vol. 80, Part 2, (1974).

Routines.Name: F3D_39
Routines.DisplayName: Right triangle to perpendicular rectangle sharing a common base. Base of right triangle is half that of rectangle
Routines.ShortDescription: Right triangle to perpendicular rectangle sharing a common base. Base of right triangle is half that of rectangle.
Routines.LongDescription: Right triangle to perpendicular rectangle sharing a common base. Base of right triangle is half that of rectangle. Function f3d_39(W,L,D) returns the view factor between a right triangle and a perpendicular rectangle that shares a common base. The base of the right triangle is half that of the rectangle. Reference: Sauer, H.J., "Configuration factors for radiant energy interchange with triangular areas," ASHRAE Transactions , Vol. 80, Part 2, (1974).

Routines.Name: F3D_40
Routines.DisplayName: Isosceles triangle to perpendicular rectangle sharing a common base
Routines.ShortDescription: Isosceles triangle to perpendicular rectangle sharing a common base.
Routines.LongDescription: Isosceles triangle to perpendicular rectangle sharing a common base. Function f3d_40(W,L,D) returns the view factor between a isosceles triangle and a perpendicular rectangle that shares a common base. Reference: Sauer, H.J., "Configuration factors for radiant energy interchange with triangular areas," ASHRAE Transactions , Vol. 80, Part 2, (1974).

Routines.Name: F3D_41
Routines.DisplayName: Right triangles that are perpendicular and share a common base. Triangle 1 has half the base length as triangle 2
Routines.ShortDescription: Right triangles that are perpendicular and share a common base. Triangle 1 has half the base length as triangle 2.
Routines.LongDescription: Right triangles that are perpendicular and share a common base. Triangle 1 has half the base length as triangle 2. Function f3d_41(W,L,D) returns the view factor between two perpendicular right triangles that share a common base. The base of triangle 1 is half that of triangle two. Reference: Sauer, H.J., "Configuration factors for radiant energy interchange with triangular areas," ASHRAE Transactions , Vol. 80, Part 2, (1974).

Routines.Name: F3D_42
Routines.DisplayName: Right triangles that are perpendicular and share a common base. Triangle 1 has half the base length as triangle 2
Routines.ShortDescription: Right triangles that are perpendicular and share a common base. Triangle 1 has half the base length as triangle 2.
Routines.LongDescription: Right triangles that are perpendicular and share a common base. Triangle 1 has half the base length as triangle 2. Function f3d_42(W,L,D) returns the view factor between two perpendicular right triangles that share a common base. The base of triangle 1 is half that of triangle two. Routines.ShortDescription: Plate to a set of cylinders that are aligned parallel normal.
Routines.LongDescription: Plate to a set of cylinders that are aligned parallel normal. Procedure f3d_71 returns the view factor from a flat plate to each of 5 cylinders that are stacked on top of one another - as shown. The calling protocol is: Call f3d_71(D, L, W, S, N_rays: F1, F2, F3, F4, F5). Reference: Brennan Fentzlaff M.S. thesis at the University of Wisconsin, to be published in 2016.

Routines.Name: F3D_72
Routines.DisplayName: Plate to a set of cylinders that are aligned perpendicular to normal
Routines.ShortDescription: Plate to a set of cylinders that are aligned perpendicular to normal.
Routines.LongDescription: Plate to a set of cylinders that are aligned perpendicular to normal. Procedure f3d_72 returns the view factor from a flat plate to each cylinder in an array that is stacked horizontally along an axis that runs parallel to the plate. The cylinders are assumed to be uniformly spaced along the plate so S = W/Ncyl. The procedure can deal with up to 10 cylinders and returns 10 outputs. The view factors Fi where i is greater than the number of cylinders are set to zero. The calling protocol is: Call f3d_72(N_rays, N_cyl, D, H, L, W: F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10). Reference: Brennan Fentzlaff M.S. thesis at the University of Wisconsin, to be published in 2016.

The cylinders are assumed to be uniformly spaced along the plate so S = L/Ncyl. The procedure can deal with up to 10 cylinders and returns 10 outputs. The view factors Fi where i is greater than the number of cylinders are set to zero. The calling protocol is: Call f3d_73(N_rays, N_cyl, D, L_cyl, L, W: F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10).
