Routines.LongDescription: Linearly-increasing Surface Temperature. The function SemiInf6(T_i, b, alpha, x, time) returns the temperature within a semi-infinite body in which the surface temperature is increasing linearly with time. Solution is from Myers (1998).

Routines.Name: SemiInf7
Routines.DisplayName: Step-change in Surface Temperature for Semi-Infinite Body Outside of Sphere
Routines.ShortDescription: Step-change in Surface Temperature for Semi-Infinite Body Outside of Sphere.
Routines.LongDescription: Step-change in Surface Temperature for Semi-Infinite Body Outside of Sphere. Function SemiInf7(T_i, T_s, alpha, a, r, time) returns the temperature within a semi-infinite that is located outside of a spherical surface and is subjected to a step change in the surface temperature. Solution is from Carslaw and Jaeger as reported in the Handbook of Heat Transfer.

Routines.Name: SemiInf8
Routines.DisplayName: Step-change in Surface Flux for Semi-Infinite Body Outside of Sphere
Routines.ShortDescription: Step-change in Surface Flux for Semi-Infinite Body Outside of Sphere.
Routines.LongDescription: Step-change in Surface Flux for Semi-Infinite Body Outside of Sphere. Function SemiInf8(T_i, q``_dot_s, alpha, k, a, r, time) returns the temperature within a semi-infinite material that is located outside of a spherical surface and is subjected to a step change in the surface heat flux. Solution is from Carslaw and Jaeger as reported in the Handbook of Heat Transfer.

Routines.Name: SemiInf9
Routines.DisplayName: Step-change in Surface Convection for Semi-Infinite Body Outside of Sphere
Routines.ShortDescription: Step-change in Surface Convection for Semi-Infinite Body Outside of Sphere.
Routines.LongDescription: Step-change in Surface Convection for Semi-Infinite Body Outside of Sphere. Function SemiInf9(T_i, h_bar, T_infinity, alpha, k, a, r, time) returns the temperature within a semi-infinite material that is located outside of a spherical surface and is subjected to a step change in the convective boundary condition at the surface. Solution is from Carslaw and Jaeger as reported in the Handbook of Heat Transfer.

Routines.Name: SemiInf10
Routines.DisplayName: Semi-infinite body with a linear initial temperature and a constant surface heat flux
Routines.ShortDescription: Semi-infinite body with a linear initial temperature and a constant surface heat flux.
Routines.LongDescription: Semi-infinite body with a linear initial temperature and a constant surface heat flux. Function SemiInf10(T_i_s, b, alpha, k, q``_dot_s, x, time) returns the temperature within a semi-infinite body with a linear initial temperature exposed to a constant heat flux.

Routines.Name: SemiInf11
Routines.DisplayName: Sinusoidally Varying Heat Flux at the Surface of a Semi-Infinite Body
Routines.ShortDescription: Sinusoidally Varying Heat Flux at the Surface of a Semi-Infinite Body.
Routines.LongDescription: Sinusoidally Varying Heat Flux at the Surface of a Semi-Infinite Body. Function SemiInf11(T_i, alpha, k, q``_dot_s, omega, x, time) returns the temperature within a semi-infinite body subjected to a sinusoidally varying surface heat flux. The quasi-steady temperature distribution is returned.

Routines.Name: SemiInf12
Routines.DisplayName: Elevated Temperature Region for Semi-Infinite Body Adjacent to the Adiabatic Surface
Routines.ShortDescription: Elevated Temperature Region for Semi-Infinite Body Adjacent to the Adiabatic Surface.
Routines.LongDescription: Elevated Temperature Region for Semi-Infinite Body Adjacent to the Adiabatic Surface. Function SemiInf12 (T_i, alpha, a, DELTAT, x, time) returns the temperature within a semi-infinite body that has an initial temperature that is non-uniform. The region immediately adjacent to the adiabatic surface (0 < x < a) is elevated by an amount DELTAT relative to the rest of the material, which is at T_i.

Routines.Name: SemiInf13
Routines.DisplayName: Elevated Temperature Region for Semi-Infinite Body Non-Adjacent to the Adiabatic Surface
Routines.ShortDescription: Elevated Temperature Region for Semi-Infinite Body Non-Adjacent to the Adiabatic Surface.
Routines.LongDescription: Elevated Temperature Region for Semi-Infinite Body Non-Adjacent to the Adiabatic Surface. Function semiinf13(T_i, alpha, a, DELTAT, x, time) returns the temperature within a semi-infinite body that has an initial temperature that is non-uniform. The region immediately adjacent to the adiabatic surface (0 < x < a) is at T_i while the remainder of the material (x>a) is elevated by an amount DELTAT. Note that the same result can be obtained by calling the function SemiInf12 with a negative DELTAT.

Routines.Name: SemiInf14
Routines.DisplayName: Elevated Temperature Region with Linear Distribution for Semi-Infinite Body Adjacent to the Adiabatic Surface
Routines.ShortDescription: Elevated Temperature Region with Linear Distribution for Semi-Infinite Body Adjacent to the Adiabatic Surface.
Routines.LongDescription: Elevated Temperature Region with Linear Distribution for Semi-Infinite Body Adjacent to the Adiabatic Surface. Function S emiInf14(T_i, alpha, a, DELTAT, x, time) returns the temperature within a semi-infinite body that has an initial temperature that is non-uniform. The region immediately adjacent to the adiabatic surface (0 < x < a) is at an elevated temperature: T = T_i+DELTAT*(1-x/a) while the remainder of the material (x>a) is at T_i.

Routines.Name: planewall_T
Routines.DisplayName: Plane Wall Temperature
Routines.ShortDescription: Plane Wall Temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: Plane Wall Temperature. Function planewall_T(x, time, T_i, T_f, alpha, k, h, L) returns the temperature ([C], [K], [F], or [R]) within a bounded plane wall exposed to convection at one surface (x=L) and adiabatic at the other surface (x=0). Notes: Function planewall_T determines the non-dimensional length, Biot and Fourier numbers and calls the function planewall_ND , which determines theta. Theta is then resolved by planewall_T into the temperature. A separation of variables technique is used to solve for the temperature, as explained in section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein .

Routines.Name: planewall_Q
Routines.DisplayName: Plane Wall Heat Transfer
Routines.ShortDescription: Plane Wall Heat Transfer.
Routines.LongDescription: Plane Wall Heat Transfer. The function planewall_Q(time, T_i, T_f, alpha, k, h, L) returns the heat transfer per unit area ([J/m^2 or Btu/ft^2]) for a bounded plane wall exposed to convection at one surface (x=L) and adiabatic at the other surface (x=0). Notes: Function planewall determines the Biot and Fourier numbers and calls the function planewall_Q_ND , which determines the non-dimensional heat transfer, Q_hat. Q_hat is then multiplied by the maximum heat transfer to obtain planewall_Q, as explained in section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein .

Routines.Name: cylinder_T
Routines.DisplayName: Cylinder Temperature
Routines.ShortDescription: Cylinder Temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: Cylinder Temperature. Function cylinder_T(r, time, T_i, T_f, alpha, k, h, r_o) returns the temperature ([C], [K], [F], or [R]) within a long right circular cylinder with the exterior walls (r=r_o) exposed to convection. Notes: Function cylinder_T determines the dimensionless length, and non-dimensional Biot and Fourier numbers. It then calls the function cylinder_T_ND which determines theta as described in Section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein . Theta is then resolved by cylinder into the temperature.

Routines.Name: cylinder_Q
Routines.DisplayName: Cylinder Heat Transfer
Routines.ShortDescription: Cylinder Heat Transfer.
Routines.LongDescription: Cylinder Heat Transfer. Function cylinder_Q(time, T_i, T_f, alpha, k, h, r_o) returns the heat transfer per unit length [J/m or Btu/ft] for a long right circular cylinder with the exterior walls (r=r_o) exposed to convection. Notes: Function cylinder_Q determines non-dimensional Biot and Fourier numbers and then calls the function cylinder_Q_ND , which determines the non-dimensional heat transfer, Q_hat, as explained in section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein.

Routines.Name: sphere_T
Routines.DisplayName: Sphere Temperature
Routines.ShortDescription: Sphere Temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: Sphere Temperature. Function sphere_T(r, time, T_i, T_f, alpha, k, h, r_o) returns the temperature ( [C], [K], [F], or [R]) within a sphere whose outer surface (r=r_o) is exposed to convection. Notes: Function sphere_T determines the dimensionless length, and non-dimensional Biot and Fourier numbers. It then calls the function sphere_T_ND , which determines theta as described in Section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein . Theta is then resolved by sphere into the temperature.

Routines.Name: sphere_Q
Routines.DisplayName: Sphere Heat Transfer
Routines.ShortDescription: Sphere Heat Transfer.
Routines.LongDescription: Sphere Heat Transfer. Function sphere_Q(time, T_i, T_f, alpha, k, h, r_o) returns the heat transfer to a sphere ([J or Btu]) whose outer surface (r=r_o) is exposed to convection. Notes: Function sphere determines non-dimensional Biot and Fourier numbers and then calls the function sphere_Q_ND which determines Q_hat, the dimensionless heat transfer as described in Section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein . The actual heat transfer is the product of Q_hat and the maximum heat transfer.

Routines.Name: planewall_T_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Plane Wall Temperature
Routines.ShortDescription: Plane Wall Temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: Plane Wall Temperature. The function planewall_T_ND(x_bar, Fo, Bi) returns the non-dimensional temperature within a bounded plane wall with one edge exposed to convection (x=L) and the other adiabatic _x=0). The supplied values, x_bar, Fo, Bi represent the dimensionless position, Fourier number and Biot number respectively. Notes: 1. Function planewall_ND is called by the function planewall to determine the non-dimensional temperature, theta. 2. The solutions provided by EES are the 1st 20 terms of the infinite series solution, as explained in section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein . 3. The result for Fo<0.001 is determine by interpolation of the solution at Fo=0.001 and the known value (the initial condition) at Fo = 0.

Routines.Name: planewall_Q_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Plane Wall Heat Transfer
Routines.ShortDescription: Plane Wall Heat Transfer.
Routines.LongDescription: Plane Wall Heat Transfer. The function planewall_Q_ND(Fo, Bi) returns the non-dimensional heat transfer to a bounded plane wall with one edge exposed to convection (x=L) and the other adiabatic (x=0). The supplied values, Fo, Bi represent the Fourier number and Biot number respectively. The non-dimensional heat transfer is the ratio of the actual to the maximum heat transfer into the wall. A separation of variables technique is used to solve for the temperature, as explained in section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein .

Routines.Name: cylinder_T_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Cylinder Temperature
Routines.ShortDescription: Cylinder Temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: Cylinder Temperature. Function cylinder_T_ND(r_bar, Fo, Bi) returns the non-dimensional temperature within a long circular cylinder with the outside edge exposed to convection (r=r_o). The supplied values, r_bar, Fo, Bi represent the dimensionless position, Fourier number and Biot number respectively. Notes: 1. Function cylinder_T_ND is called by the function cylinder_T to determine the non-dimensional temperature, theta, as explained in section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein. 2. The solutions provided by EES are the 1st 20 terms of the infinite series solution 3. The result for Fo<0.001 is determine by interpolation of the solution at Fo=0.001 and the known value (the initial condition) at Fo = 0.

Routines.Name: cylinder_Q_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Cylinder Heat Transfer
Routines.ShortDescription: Cylinder Heat Transfer.
Routines.LongDescription: Cylinder Heat Transfer. Function cylinder_Q_ND(Fo, Bi) returns the non-dimensional heat transfer within a long circular cylinder with the outside edge exposed to convection (r=r_o). The supplied values, Fo, Bi represent the Fourier number and Biot number respectively. A separation of variable technique is used as described in Section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein .

Routines.Name: sphere_T_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Sphere Temperature
Routines.ShortDescription: Sphere Temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: Sphere Temperature. Function sphere_T_ND(r_bar, Fo, Bi) returns the non-dimensional temperature within a sphere whose outer surface (r=r_o) is exposed to convection. The supplied values, r_bar, Fo, Bi represent the dimensionless position, Fourier number and Biot number respectively. Notes: 1. Function sphere_T_ND is called by the function sphere_T to determine the non-dimensional temperature, theta, as described in Section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein . 2. The solutions provided by EES are the 1st 20 terms of the infinite series solution 3. The result for Fo<0.001 is determine by interpolation of the solution at Fo=0.001 and the known value (the initial condition) at Fo = 0.

Routines.Name: sphere_Q_ND
Routines.DisplayName: Sphere Heat Transfer
Routines.ShortDescription: Sphere Heat Transfer.
Routines.LongDescription: Sphere Heat Transfer. The function sphere_Q_ND(Fo, Bi) returns the non-dimensional heat transfer into a sphere whose outer surface (r=r_o) is exposed to convection. The supplied values, Fo, Bi represent Fourier number and Biot number respectively. See Section 3.5.2 of Nellis and Klein for more information.

Routines.Name: Combustor1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Combustor 1
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a combustor using a specified heat of combustion and air-fuel ratio.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Combustor1_CL is a model of a combustor such as used in gas turbine systems. This model does not do combustion calculations, but rather, it accepts the heat of combustion of the fuel and the air-fuel ratio. Combustor2 is a similar model but it does the combustion calculations.

Routines.Name: Combustor2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Combustor 2
Routines.ShortDescription: Models complete combustion with dry air and a specified percentage of excess air.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Combustor2_CL provides a model of a combustor. It accepts the name of the fuel, which must be a name contained in the list of ideal and NASA gases. The procedure assumes complete combustion with dry air. The percentage of excess air above the stoichiometric requirement is provided in input Excess%. The combustion process is assumed to be adiabatic if eta is 1. If eta is less than 1, then some of the energy provided in the combustion process is assumed to be lost to the surrounding through the combustor jacket. The loss is calculated using the lower heating value of the fuel as the basis; that is (1-eta)*Q_dot_f is the jacket loss. The fuel is assumed to be supplied at a reference temperature of 25C (77F). The procedure calculates the outlet temperature of the products. The procedure also returns the mass flow rate of the fluid multiplied by its lower heating value as well as the rate at which energy would be transferred if the products were cooled from their outlet temperature to the inlet temperature of the air used for combustion.

Routines.Name: Combustor3_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Combustor 3
Routines.ShortDescription: Models equilibrium combustion with dissociation using air or oxygen.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Combustor3_CL provides a model of a combustor. It accepts the name of the fuel, which can be a name contained in the list of ideal and NASA gases or any chemical formula consisting of elements C, H, O, N, and S. The procedure assumes complete combustion with dry air or pure oxygen. No fuel or fuel fragments remain. The percentage of excess air (or oxygen) above the stoichiometric requirement is provided in input Excess%. At the elevated temperatures occurring in a combustion process, dissociation reactions that produce CO, NO, OH and other species can occur to a significant extent and they affect the outlet temperature of the combustion of the product gas. This model is specifically designed to consider dissociation reactions. The product gas is assumed to be a mixture of CO2, CO, H2O, H, H2, OH, O, O2 ,NO, NO2, N2, N, SO2 and SO3 and the equilibrium mole fractions of these gases are determined in the analysis. The fuel is assumed to be supplied at the same temperature as the air. Some of the energy released in the combustion process may be transferred to the surrounding through the combustor jacket. The rate of energy transfer from the combustion chamber is calculated as the product of a Conductance and the difference in temperature between the outlet gas and in the inlet air. The procedure returns the this energy transfer rate and the rate of energy transfer that would occur if the combustion gases were cooled from their outlet temperature to the inlet temperature of the air used for combustion. An efficiency (Eff) is determined as the ratio of the energy in the product gas to the lower heating value of the fuel. Note that, even when the Conductance is 0 so that there are no energy losses from the combustion chamber, Eff may be less than one as a result of the dissociation reactions.

Routines.Name: Combustor4_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Combustor 4
Routines.ShortDescription: Calculates combustor heat transfer for a specified equilibrium outlet temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Combustor4_CL provides a model of a combustor is similar to Combustor3_CL with the major difference being that it accepts the outlet equilibrium temperature and calculates the heat transfer rate to the combustion chamber. As with Combustor3_CL, this component accepts the name of the fuel, which can be a name contained in the list of ideal and NASA gases or any chemical formula consisting of elements C, H, O, N, and S. The procedure assumes complete combustion with dry air or pure oxygen. No fuel or fuel fragments remain. The percentage of excess air (or oxygen) above the stoichiometric requirement is provided in input Excess%. At the elevated temperatures occurring in a combustion process, dissociation reactions that produce CO, NO, OH and other species can occur to a significant extent. This model is specifically designed to consider dissociation reactions. The product gas is assumed to be a mixture of CO2, CO, H2O, H, H2, OH, O, O2 ,NO, NO2, N2, N, SO2 and SO3 and the equilibrium mole fractions of these gases are determined in the analysis. The heat transfer rate from the combustion vessel is an output of this component. The fuel is assumed to be supplied at the same temperature as the air. A negative heat transfer rate indicates energy needs to be transferred to the equilibrium gas mixture to achieve the specified outlet temperature.

Routines.Name: Compressor1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Single-stage radial compressor
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a single-stage radial compressor using shifted head and efficiency curves.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Compressor1_CL models a single-stage radial compressor operating outside the vapor dome. Pressure rise is determined from a generic head-coefficient versus flow-coefficient curve, and efficiency is determined from a generic efficiency versus flow-coefficient curve. The curves can be shifted vertically and horizontally using the supplied maximum values and flow scaling. The correlations are based on the radial compressor model described by Dyreby (2014).

Routines.Name: Compressor2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Constant isentropic or polytropic efficiency
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a compressor with a specified isentropic or polytropic efficiency.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Compressor2_CL models a compressor with a specified isentropic or polytropic efficiency and operates both within and outside the vapor dome. A positive value of eta is interpreted as isentropic efficiency, while the absolute value of a negative eta is interpreted as polytropic efficiency.

Routines.Name: Compressor3_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Reciprocating refrigeration compressor
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a reciprocating compressor for refrigeration and air-conditioning applications.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Compressor3_CL models a reciprocating compressor used in refrigeration and air-conditioning applications. The model determines volumetric efficiency, refrigerant mass flow rate, compressor power, and outlet enthalpy from displacement, clearance, operating temperatures, intake-valve pressure loss, and combined compressor-motor efficiency. The method is based on Jahnig, Reindl, and Klein, ASHRAE Transactions, Vol. 106, Part 2 (2000).

Routines.Name: Compressor4_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Scroll refrigeration compressor
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a scroll compressor for refrigeration and air-conditioning applications.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Compressor4_CL models a scroll compressor used in refrigeration and air-conditioning applications. A leakage coefficient determines volumetric efficiency and an overall compressor-motor efficiency determines input power. A negative value for either parameter selects a default correlation based on compressor calorimeter data from Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

Routines.Name: Compressor5_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Efficiency from specific speed and diameter
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns compressor isentropic efficiency from specific speed and specific diameter.
Routines.LongDescription: Function Compressor5_CL returns compressor isentropic efficiency for a specified specific speed and specific diameter. The function uses a curve fit to the Balje curves. The optional eta_max adjustment is represented by the required third argument; set it to a negative value to retain the Balje-curve maximum efficiency.

Routines.Name: Compressor6_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Optimal specific diameter from specific speed
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the optimal compressor specific diameter for a specified specific speed.
Routines.LongDescription: Function Compressor6_CL returns the optimal compressor specific diameter for a specified specific speed. The function uses a curve fit to the peak of the Balje curves so that the result remains on the peak-efficiency locus.

Routines.Name: DuctSuddenExp_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Sudden Expansion
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a sudden expansion given the fluid, its flow rate and state and the upstream and downstream areas. This function calls the K_sudden_expansion function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a sudden expansion given the fluid, its flow rate and state and the upstream and downstream areas. This function calls the K_sudden_expansion function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctGradualExpansion_Long_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Gradual Expansions with Long Discharge
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a gradual expansion with a long discharge duct length given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the upstream and downstream areas, and the half angle. Valid for both rectangular and circular duct cross-sections. This function calls the K_gradual_expansion2 function from the minor loss library. Note that a sudden contraction can be simulated by using a half-angle greater than 45 degree.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a gradual expansion with a long discharge duct length given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the upstream and downstream areas, and the half angle. Valid for both rectangular and circular duct cross-sections. This function calls the K_gradual_expansion2 function from the minor loss library. Note that a sudden contraction can be simulated by using a half-angle greater than 45 degree.

Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a gradual expansion with no discharge duct length given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the upstream and downstream areas, and the half angle. Valid for circular duct cross-sections. This function calls the K_grad_exp_circ_free function from the minor loss library.

Valid for rectangular duct cross-sections. This function calls the K_grad_exp_rect_free function from the minor loss library.

Routines.DisplayName: Sudden Contraction
Routines.ShortDescription: $VarInfo DP units=Pa.
Routines.LongDescription: $VarInfo DP units=Pa. Returns the pressure drop associated with a sudden contraction given the fluid, its flow rate and state and the upstream and downstream areas. This function calls the K_sudden_contraction function from the minor loss library.

Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop in a rectangular duct bend given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the width and height of the duct, the bend radius, and the turning angle. This function calls the function K_Bend_Rect from the minor loss category of the heat transfer library.

The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in the main duct. The function calls the K_supply_main function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctSupplyMain90B_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Supply branch - main, Lindab
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a supply duct with a branch. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in the main duct. The function uses the information from the Lindab web site.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a supply duct with a branch. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in the main duct. The function uses the information from the Lindab web site.

Routines.Name: DuctSupplyTee_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Supply branch, tee - circular
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a supply duct with an equal area tee. The ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in branch 1. The function calls the K_supply_tee function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a supply duct with an equal area tee. The ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in branch 1. The function calls the K_supply_tee function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctSupplyTeeB_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Supply branch, tee - circular, Lindab
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a supply duct with an equal area tee. The ducts have circular cross-section. The function uses information from the Lindab web site.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a supply duct with an equal area tee. The ducts have circular cross-section. The function uses information from the Lindab web site.

Routines.Name: DuctExtractBranch45_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Extract branch 45 degree circular - branch
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 45 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow from the branch. The function calls the K_extract_branch_45 function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 45 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow from the branch. The function calls the K_extract_branch_45 function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctExtractMain45_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Extract branch 45 degree circular - main
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 45 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in the main duct. The function calls the K_extract_main_45 function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 45 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in the main duct. The function calls the K_extract_main_45 function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctExtractBranch90_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Extract branch 90 degree circular - branch
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 90 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow from the branch. The function calls the K_extract_branch_90 function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 90 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow from the branch. The function calls the K_extract_branch_90 function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctExtractBranch90B_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Extract branch 90 degree circular - branch, Lindab
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 90 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow from the branch. The function uses the information from the Lindab website.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 90 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow from the branch. The function uses the information from the Lindab website.

Routines.Name: DuctExtractMain90_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Extract branch 90 degree circular - main
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 90 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in the main duct. The function calls the K_extract_main_90 function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 90 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in the main duct. The function calls the K_extract_main_90 function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctExtractMain90B_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Extract branch 90 degree circular - main, Lindab
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 90 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in the main duct. The function uses the information from the Lindab web site. Ducts 2 and 3 have the same diameter.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with a branch. The branch is at 90 degrees and the ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in the main duct. The function uses the information from the Lindab web site. Ducts 2 and 3 have the same diameter.

Routines.Name: DuctExtractTee_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Extract branch, tee - circular
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with an equal area tee. The ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in branch 1. The function calls the K_extract_tee function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with an equal area tee. The ducts have circular cross-section. The pressure drop should be applied to the flow in branch 1. The function calls the K_extract_tee function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctExtractTeeB_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Extract branch, tee - Lindab
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with an equal area tee with equal flow in the two incoming branches. The ducts have circular cross-section. The function uses the information from the Lindab website for a T-piece.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with an extract duct with an equal area tee with equal flow in the two incoming branches. The ducts have circular cross-section. The function uses the information from the Lindab website for a T-piece.

Routines.Name: DuctRoundedInlet_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Rounded Duct Inlet
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a rounded inlet given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the radius of the inlet and the diameter of the pipe. Valid for circular duct cross-sections. This function calls the K_Rounded_Pipe_Inlet function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a rounded inlet given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the radius of the inlet and the diameter of the pipe. Valid for circular duct cross-sections. This function calls the K_Rounded_Pipe_Inlet function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctReentrantInlet_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Reentrant Duct Inlet
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a reentrant inlet given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the length of reentrant duct, the duct wall thickness, and the diameter of the duct. Valid for circular duct cross-sections. This function calls the K_Reentrant_Pipe_Inlet function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a reentrant inlet given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the length of reentrant duct, the duct wall thickness, and the diameter of the duct. Valid for circular duct cross-sections. This function calls the K_Reentrant_Pipe_Inlet function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctDamperParallel_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Parallel Vane
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a damper that has parallel vanes given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the upstream area, and the vane angle. This function calls the K_damper_parallel function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a damper that has parallel vanes given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the upstream area, and the vane angle. This function calls the K_damper_parallel function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctDamperOpposed_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Opposed Vane
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a damper that has opposed vanes given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the upstream area, and the vane angle. This function calls the K_damper_opposed function from the minor loss library.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a damper that has opposed vanes given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the upstream area, and the vane angle. This function calls the K_damper_opposed function from the minor loss library.

Routines.Name: DuctRoundFriction_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Length of Round Duct
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a length of round duct given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the diameter and length of the duct. This function calls the PipeFlow function from the heat transfer library assuming a smooth wall.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a length of round duct given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the diameter and length of the duct. This function calls the PipeFlow function from the heat transfer library assuming a smooth wall.

Routines.Name: DuctRectFriction_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Length of Rectangular Duct
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a length of rectangular duct given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the width, height and length of the duct. This function calls the DuctFlow function from the heat transfer library assuming a smooth wall.
Routines.LongDescription: Returns the pressure drop associated with a length of rectangular duct given the fluid, its flow rate and state, the width, height and length of the duct. This function calls the DuctFlow function from the heat transfer library assuming a smooth wall.

Routines.Name: Fan1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Vane Axial Fan
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a vane-axial fan using dimensionless pressure-rise, flow-rate, and power curves.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Fan1_CL provides a model of a vane-axial fan based on dimensionless pressure-rise and power curves as functions of dimensionless volumetric flow rate. The curves were generated by collapsing performance data from several fan manufacturers and models.

Routines.Name: Fan2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Straight-Blade Centrifugal Fan
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a straight-blade centrifugal fan using dimensionless performance curves.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Fan2_CL provides a model of a straight-blade centrifugal fan based on dimensionless pressure-rise and power curves as functions of dimensionless volumetric flow rate. The curves were generated by collapsing performance data from the Greenheck USF Centrifugal Fan Performance Supplement.

Routines.Name: Fan3_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Airfoil-Blade Centrifugal Fan
Routines.ShortDescription: Models an airfoil-blade centrifugal fan using dimensionless performance curves.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Fan3_CL provides a model of an airfoil-blade centrifugal fan based on dimensionless pressure-rise and power curves as functions of dimensionless volumetric flow rate. The curves were generated by collapsing performance data from the Greenheck USF Centrifugal Fan Performance Supplement.

Routines.Name: AngleValve_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Angle Valve
Routines.ShortDescription: Models pressure change through an angle valve.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure AngleValve_CL models an angle valve. The valve resistance coefficient is obtained from the K_AngleValve procedure using the correlation published in Crane Technical Paper 410M.

Routines.Name: GateValve_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Gate Valve
Routines.ShortDescription: Models pressure change through a gate valve.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure GateValve_CL models a gate valve. The valve resistance coefficient is obtained from the K_GateValve procedure using the correlation published in Crane Technical Paper 410M.

Routines.Name: GlobeValve_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Globe Valve
Routines.ShortDescription: Models pressure change through a globe valve.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure GlobeValve_CL models a globe valve. The valve resistance coefficient is obtained from the K_GlobeValve procedure using the correlation published in Crane Technical Paper 410M.

Routines.Name: SwingCheckValve_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Swing Check Valve
Routines.ShortDescription: Models pressure change through a swing check valve.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure SwingCheckValve_CL models a swing-type check valve. The valve resistance coefficient is obtained from the K_SwingCheckValve procedure using the correlation published in Crane Technical Paper 410M.

Routines.Name: CapTube1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Capillary Tube (adiabatic)
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines refrigerant mass flow through an adiabatic capillary tube.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure CapTube1_CL determines mass flow rate through an adiabatic capillary tube using the empirical relation published in Chapter 11 of the 2014 ASHRAE Refrigeration Handbook.

Routines.Name: Restrictor1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Short-tube restrictor with sharp-edge inlet
Routines.ShortDescription: Estimates refrigerant mass flow through a sharp-edged short-tube restrictor.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Restrictor1_CL estimates mass flow rate through a sharp-edged short-tube restrictor with L/D ratios between 4 and 30 for use in refrigeration cycles.

Routines.Name: Restrictor2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Short-tube restrictor with chamfer inlet
Routines.ShortDescription: Estimates refrigerant mass flow through a chamfered short-tube restrictor.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Restrictor2_CL estimates mass flow rate through a chamfered short-tube restrictor with L/D ratios between 4 and 30 for use in refrigeration cycles.

Routines.Name: ValveCoef_Inc_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Simple incompressible valve coefficient calculator
Routines.ShortDescription: Calculates valve coefficients for incompressible flow using simplified sizing equations.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure ValveCoef_Inc_CL uses simplified sizing equations to determine the valve coefficients C_v and K_v for incompressible flow from the flow conditions, pressure drop, and required flow rate.

Routines.Name: ValveCoef_Inc_ISA75_CL
Routines.DisplayName: ISA 75 incompressible valve coefficient calculator
Routines.ShortDescription: Calculates incompressible-flow valve coefficients using ANSI/ISA-75 sizing relations.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure ValveCoef_Inc_ISA75_CL applies the detailed ANSI/ISA-75.01.01 valve-sizing relations to determine C_v and K_v for incompressible flow from the conditions, geometry, valve factors, pressure drop, and flow rate.

Routines.Name: ValveCoef_Comp_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Simple compressible valve coefficient calculator
Routines.ShortDescription: Calculates valve coefficients for compressible flow using simplified sizing equations.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure ValveCoef_Comp_CL uses simplified sizing equations to determine the valve coefficients C_v and K_v for compressible flow from the flow conditions, pressure drop, and required standard-condition flow rate.

Routines.Name: ValveCoef_Comp_ISA75_CL
Routines.DisplayName: ISA 75 compressible valve coefficient calculator
Routines.ShortDescription: Calculates compressible-flow valve coefficients using ANSI/ISA-75 sizing relations.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure ValveCoef_Comp_ISA75_CL applies the detailed ANSI/ISA-75.01.01 valve-sizing relations to determine C_v and K_v for compressible flow from the conditions, geometry, valve factors, pressure drop, and standard-condition flow rate.

Routines.Name: ValveSizing_ISA75_Tab
Routines.DisplayName: ISA 75 valve coefficient calculator toolbox
Routines.ShortDescription: Provides an EES toolbox tab for ISA 75 valve sizing calculations.
Routines.LongDescription: This EES toolbox tab implements detailed ANSI/ISA-75.01.01 sizing relations for compressible and incompressible control-valve flow. It determines C_v and K_v from flow conditions, geometry, valve type, pressure drop, and required flow rate, and also includes a simplified sizing method.

Routines.Name: CoolingCoil1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Cooling coil using chilled water as the coolant
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a humid-air cooling coil using chilled water as the coolant.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure CoolingCoil1_CL models a heat exchanger that cools humid air with chilled water. It detects condensation and applies dry- or wet-coil heat and mass transfer relations to determine heat transfer, outlet temperatures, and condensate removal.

Routines.Name: CoolingCoil2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Cooling coil using brine as the coolant
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a humid-air cooling coil using a brine solution as the coolant.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure CoolingCoil2_CL models a heat exchanger that cools humid air with an EES brine solution. It detects condensation and applies dry- or wet-coil heat and mass transfer relations to determine heat transfer, outlet temperatures, and condensate removal.

Routines.Name: CoolingTower1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Cooling tower using analogy method
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a counterflow cooling tower using the heat and mass transfer analogy method.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure CoolingTower1_CL determines counterflow cooling-tower performance using an analogy method and an enthalpy effectiveness based on the air-to-water heat transfer conductance. It returns outlet water temperature, makeup-water rate, capacity, range, and approach.

Routines.Name: EnthalpyExchanger1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Enthalpy exchanger with Preheat Control
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a rotary enthalpy exchanger with condensation-avoidance preheat control.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure EnthalpyExchanger1_CL models heat and water-vapor exchange between outdoor supply air and indoor exhaust air in a rotary enthalpy exchanger. It includes a preheat control strategy that raises supply-air temperature when needed to avoid exhaust-air condensation.

Routines.Name: EvaporativeCondenser1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Evaporative condenser design (determine A_R)
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines the refrigerant-side area required for an evaporative condenser.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure EvaporativeCondenser1_CL determines the refrigerant-side surface area required to condense a refrigerant from a saturated or superheated inlet state to a saturated or subcooled liquid state. Wetted-surface heat transfer enhancement is calculated internally.

Routines.Name: EvaporativeCondenser2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Evaporative condenser (determine outlet states)
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines evaporative-condenser outlet states for a specified refrigerant-side area.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure EvaporativeCondenser2_CL determines outlet refrigerant and air states for an evaporative condenser with a specified refrigerant-side surface area. The refrigerant inlet may be two-phase or superheated, and wetted-surface heat transfer enhancement is calculated internally.

Routines.Name: HeatExchanger1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Heat exchange between a single phase fluid and reservoir 1
Routines.ShortDescription: Models heat exchange between a single-phase fluid and a thermal reservoir.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure HeatExchanger1_CL determines outlet state, pressure, heat transfer rate, and effectiveness for a single-phase fluid exchanging heat with a constant-temperature reservoir at a specified approach temperature and fractional pressure drop.

Routines.Name: HeatExchanger2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Heat exchange between two single phase fluids - specified approach
Routines.ShortDescription: Models heat exchange between two single-phase fluid streams at a specified approach.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure HeatExchanger2_CL determines both outlet states, outlet pressures, heat transfer rate, and effectiveness for two single-phase streams using a specified minimum approach temperature and fractional pressure drops.

Routines.Name: HeatExchanger3_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Heat exchange between a single phase liquid and gas using compact HX library
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a compact liquid-to-gas heat exchanger from geometry and flow conditions.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure HeatExchanger3_CL uses Compact Heat Exchanger Library geometry to determine outlet states, pressure drops, heat transfer rate, effectiveness, number of transfer units, and fin efficiency for a single-phase liquid and gas.

Routines.Name: HeatExchanger4_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Counterflow recuperator with sub-heat exchanger model, UA given
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a counterflow recuperator for a specified overall conductance.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure HeatExchanger4_CL divides a counterflow recuperator into sub-heat exchangers and determines outlet enthalpies, effectiveness, and pinch-point temperature difference for a specified UA.

Routines.Name: HeatExchanger5_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Counterflow recuperator with sub-heat exchanger model, effectiveness given
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a counterflow recuperator for a specified effectiveness.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure HeatExchanger5_CL divides a counterflow recuperator into sub-heat exchangers and determines outlet enthalpies, required UA, and pinch-point temperature difference for a specified effectiveness.

Routines.Name: HeatExchanger6_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Counterflow recuperator with sub-heat exchanger model, DT_pp given
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a counterflow recuperator for a specified pinch-point difference.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure HeatExchanger6_CL divides a counterflow recuperator into sub-heat exchangers and determines outlet enthalpies, required UA, and effectiveness for a specified pinch-point temperature difference.

Routines.Name: Condenser1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Air-cooled condenser design (determine UA)
Routines.ShortDescription: Designs an air-cooled condenser from specified heat transfer coefficients.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Condenser1_CL determines the refrigerant-side area, overall conductance, heat transfer rate, outlet states, and phase-region area fractions for an air-cooled condenser with specified heat transfer coefficients.

Routines.Name: Condenser2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Air-cooled condenser (determine outlet state)
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines air-cooled condenser outlet states for a specified area.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Condenser2_CL determines heat transfer rate, refrigerant and air outlet states, and phase-region area fractions for an air-cooled condenser with specified refrigerant-side area and heat transfer coefficients.

Routines.Name: Condenser3_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Air-cooled condenser design (determine L)
Routines.ShortDescription: Designs an air-cooled condenser using compact heat exchanger geometry.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Condenser3_CL determines required length, refrigerant-side area, conductance, heat transfer, outlet states, air pressure drop, and phase-region fractions using Compact Heat Exchanger Library geometry.

Routines.Name: Condenser4_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Air-cooled condenser (determine outlet state)
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines air-cooled condenser outlet states from compact-HX geometry.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Condenser4_CL determines heat transfer rate, refrigerant and air outlet states, and air-side pressure drop for an air-cooled condenser with specified compact heat exchanger geometry and length.

Routines.Name: Condenser5_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Liquid-cooled condenser design (determine Area)
Routines.ShortDescription: Designs a liquid-cooled condenser for a specified outlet subcooling.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Condenser5_CL determines refrigerant-side area, overall conductance, heat transfer rate, outlet states, and phase-region area fractions for a liquid-cooled condenser.

Routines.Name: Condenser6_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Liquid-cooled condenser (determine outlet state)
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines liquid-cooled condenser outlet states for a specified area.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Condenser6_CL determines heat transfer rate, refrigerant and coolant outlet states, and phase-region area fractions for a liquid-cooled condenser with specified refrigerant-side area.

Routines.Name: Evaporator1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Air-cooled evaporator design (determine UA)
Routines.ShortDescription: Designs an air-cooled evaporator from specified heat transfer coefficients.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Evaporator1_CL determines refrigerant-side area, overall conductance, heat transfer rate, outlet states, and superheated area fraction for an air-cooled evaporator at a specified outlet superheat.

Routines.Name: Evaporator2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Air-cooled evaporator (determine outlet state)
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines air-cooled evaporator outlet states for a specified area.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Evaporator2_CL determines heat transfer rate and refrigerant and air outlet states for an air-cooled evaporator with specified refrigerant-side area and heat transfer coefficients.

Routines.Name: Evaporator3_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Air-cooled evaporator design (determine L)
Routines.ShortDescription: Designs an air-cooled evaporator using compact heat exchanger geometry.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Evaporator3_CL determines required length, refrigerant-side area, conductance, heat transfer, outlet states, air pressure drop, and superheated area fraction using Compact Heat Exchanger Library geometry.

Routines.Name: Evaporator4_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Air-cooled evaporator (determine outlet state)
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines air-cooled evaporator outlet states from compact-HX geometry.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Evaporator4_CL determines heat transfer rate, refrigerant and air outlet states, and air-side pressure drop for an air-cooled evaporator with specified compact heat exchanger geometry and length.

Routines.Name: Evaporator5_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Liquid-cooled evaporator design (determine area)
Routines.ShortDescription: Designs a liquid-cooled evaporator for a specified outlet superheat.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Evaporator5_CL determines refrigerant-side area, overall conductance, heat transfer rate, outlet states, and superheated area fraction for a liquid-cooled evaporator.

Routines.Name: Evaporator6_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Liquid-cooled evaporator (determine outlet state)
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines liquid-cooled evaporator outlet states for a specified area.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Evaporator6_CL determines heat transfer rate and refrigerant and coolant outlet states for a liquid-cooled evaporator with specified refrigerant-side area.

Routines.Name: GearPump3_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Gear Pump 3
Routines.ShortDescription: Models gear-pump pressure rise, power, and efficiency from pump geometry and operating conditions.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure GearPump3_CL models a gear pump using displacement, leakage and friction parameters, operating speed, inlet state, and mass flow rate. It returns pressure rise, shaft power, pump efficiency, and volumetric efficiency.

Routines.Name: GearPump4_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Gear Pump 4
Routines.ShortDescription: Determines gear-pump model parameters from two measured operating points.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure GearPump4_CL uses two measured gear-pump operating points to determine displacement, leakage and friction parameters, and an overall efficiency parameter for use with the gear-pump component model.

Routines.Name: CentrifugalPump1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Centrifugal Pump 1
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a centrifugal pump from inlet conditions, flow rate, speed, and impeller geometry.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure CentrifugalPump1_CL models a centrifugal pump using fluid state, mass flow rate, rotational speed, impeller diameter, and hub diameter. It returns outlet pressure and temperature, required shaft power, and pump efficiency.

Routines.Name: Turbine1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Low reaction, single-stage radial turbine
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a low-reaction, single-stage radial turbine.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Turbine1_CL models a low-reaction, single-stage radial turbine from inlet and outlet pressures, inlet temperature, fluid, rotational speed, geometry, and efficiency scaling inputs. It returns mass flow rate, outlet temperature, power, velocity ratio, efficiency, and Mach number.

Routines.Name: Turbine2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Constant isentropic or polytropic efficiency
Routines.ShortDescription: Models turbine expansion with a specified isentropic or polytropic efficiency.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Turbine2_CL determines the outlet enthalpy, turbine power, and isentropic efficiency for a specified inlet state, outlet pressure, mass flow rate, fluid, and constant isentropic or polytropic efficiency.

Routines.Name: Turbine3_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Efficiency given the specific speed and diameter
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns turbine efficiency from specific speed and specific diameter.
Routines.LongDescription: Function Turbine3_CL estimates turbine efficiency from specific speed, specific diameter, and a specified maximum efficiency.

Routines.Name: Turbine4_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Optimal specific diameter given specific speed
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the optimal turbine specific diameter for a specified specific speed.
Routines.LongDescription: Function Turbine4_CL estimates the optimal turbine specific diameter corresponding to a specified specific speed.

Routines.Name: Nozzle1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Nozzle 1
Routines.ShortDescription: Models expansion through a nozzle with a specified efficiency.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Nozzle1_CL determines nozzle outlet enthalpy, velocity, and Mach number from inlet enthalpy, inlet pressure and velocity, outlet pressure, fluid, and nozzle efficiency.

Routines.Name: CDNozzle1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: CD Nozzle 1
Routines.ShortDescription: Models flow through a converging-diverging nozzle for specified throat and exit areas.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure CDNozzle1_CL determines the exit temperature, pressure, Mach number, and velocity for a gas flowing through a converging-diverging nozzle with specified throat and outlet areas.

Routines.Name: CDNozzle2_CL
Routines.DisplayName: CD Nozzle 2
Routines.ShortDescription: Models a converging-diverging nozzle and evaluates exit and critical pressures.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure CDNozzle2_CL determines exit pressure, Mach number, temperature, and velocity for a converging-diverging nozzle and also returns the critical and design pressures for the specified geometry and flow state.

Routines.Name: Diffuser1_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Diffuser 1
Routines.ShortDescription: Models diffusion to a specified outlet velocity with a specified efficiency.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Diffuser1_CL determines outlet enthalpy, outlet pressure, and pressure-recovery coefficient for a diffuser from the inlet state and velocity, specified outlet velocity, fluid, and diffuser efficiency.

Routines.Name: Shock_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Shock wave
Routines.ShortDescription: Calculates the downstream state across a normal shock wave.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure Shock_CL determines downstream pressure, enthalpy, and Mach number across a shock wave from the upstream fluid, pressure, enthalpy, and Mach number.

Routines.Name: EjectorPump_CL
Routines.DisplayName: Ejector Pump
Routines.ShortDescription: Models an ejector pump using primary and secondary inlet states and component efficiencies.
Routines.LongDescription: Procedure EjectorPump_CL models an ejector pump from primary-nozzle diameter, primary and secondary inlet states, nozzle, mixing, and diffuser efficiencies, nozzle pressure, and entrainment ratio. It returns primary and secondary mass flow rates and the mixed outlet pressure and enthalpy.

Routines.Name: Surface_Factor
Routines.DisplayName: Surface Modifier
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the Marin endurance-limit modification factor for surface finish.
Routines.LongDescription: Function Surface_Factor returns the dimensionless Marin surface factor k_a from ultimate tensile strength and a specified surface finish. The factor is limited to 1 when the correlation would otherwise produce a larger value.

Routines.Name: Size_Factor_Round_Rotating
Routines.DisplayName: Size Modifier Round Rotating
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the Marin size factor for a round rotating member.

Routines.Name: Loading_factor
Routines.DisplayName: Loading Modifier

Routines.LongDescription: Function Loading_factor returns the dimensionless Marin loading factor k_c for axial, bending, or torsional loading.

Routines.Name: Temperature_factor
Routines.DisplayName: Temperature Modifier
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the Marin temperature factor for steel endurance-limit calculations.
Routines.LongDescription: Function Temperature_factor returns the dimensionless Marin temperature factor k_d for steel when temperature-dependent ultimate strength is unavailable. The documented range is 20 C to 500 C.

Routines.Name: Reliability_factor
Routines.DisplayName: Reliability Modifier
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the Marin reliability factor for a specified confidence level.
Routines.LongDescription: Function Reliability_factor returns the dimensionless Marin reliability factor k_e to account for fatigue-data scatter and provide a specified confidence level. The documented relation assumes an 8 percent standard deviation and a 50 percent unmodified reliability.

Routines.Name: Notch_Sensitivity

Routines.LongDescription: Function Notch_Sensitivity returns the dimensionless notch sensitivity q for aluminum alloys, steels, or cast irons under axial, bending, or torsional loading. The result can be used with the static stress-concentration factor to calculate the fatigue stress-concentration factor.

Routines.Name: gear_Lewis_factor

Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for plate with opposed u-shaped notches under tension.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_1 returns the stress concentration factor for a plate with two opposed U-shaped notches along its length. The plate is subject to axial tension along its length.

Routines.Name: SCF_2
Routines.DisplayName: Plate with opposed u-shaped notches under bending
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for plate with opposed u-shaped notches under bending.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_2 returns the stress concentration factor for a plate with two opposed U-shaped notches along its length. The plate is subject to bending moments in the plane of the plate.

Routines.Name: SCF_3
Routines.DisplayName: Rod with u-shaped groove under tension
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for rod with u-shaped groove under tension.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_3 returns the stress concentration factor for a rod of diameter D with a circumscribing U-shaped groove. The rod is under axial tension.

Routines.Name: SCF_4
Routines.DisplayName: Rod with u-shaped groove under bending
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for rod with u-shaped groove under bending.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_4 returns the stress concentration factor for a rod of diameter D with a circumscribing U-shaped groove. The rod is subject to bending moments.

Routines.Name: SCF_5
Routines.DisplayName: Rod with u-shaped groove under torsion
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for rod with u-shaped groove under torsion.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_5 returns the stress concentration factor for a rod of diameter D with a circumscribing U-shaped groove. The rod is under torsion.

Routines.Name: SCF_6
Routines.DisplayName: Plate with shoulder fillets under tension
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for plate with shoulder fillets under tension.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_6 returns the stress concentration factor for a plate with shouldered fillets on both sides. The plate is subject to axial tension along its length.

Routines.Name: SCF_7
Routines.DisplayName: Plate with shoulder fillets under bending
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for plate with shoulder fillets under bending.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_7 returns the stress concentration factor for a plate with shouldered fillets on both sides. The plate is subject to bending moments in the plane of the plate.

Routines.Name: SCF_8
Routines.DisplayName: Rod with shoulder fillets under tension
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for rod with shoulder fillets under tension.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_8 returns the stress concentration factor for a stepped bar with shoulder fillets. The rod is subject to axial tension.

Routines.Name: SCF_9
Routines.DisplayName: Rod with shoulder fillets under bending
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for rod with shoulder fillets under bending.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_9 returns the stress concentration factor for a stepped bar with shoulder fillets. The rod is subject to bending moments.

Routines.Name: SCF_10
Routines.DisplayName: Rod with shoulder fillets under torsion
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for rod with shoulder fillets under torsion.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_10 returns the stress concentration factor for a stepped bar with shoulder fillets. The rod is subject to torsion.

Routines.Name: SCF_11
Routines.DisplayName: Plate with centered hole under tension
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for plate with centered hole under tension.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_11 returns the stress concentration factor for a plate with centered hole of diameter d. The plate is subject to axial tension along its length.

Routines.Name: SCF_12
Routines.DisplayName: Plate with centered hole under simple bending
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for plate with centered hole under simple bending.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_12 returns the stress concentration factor for a plate with a centered hole under simple bending. The moment should be specified with units of moments/length.

Routines.Name: SCF_13
Routines.DisplayName: Plate with centered hole under cylindrical bending
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for plate with centered hole under cylindrical bending.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_13 returns the stress concentration factor for a plate with a centered hole subject to cylindrical bending. The moment M_2 is based on Poisson's ratio and is estimated at a value of 30% of M_1. Both M_1 and M_2 are distributed moments with units of moments/length.

Routines.Name: SCF_14
Routines.DisplayName: Plate with eccentric hole under tension
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for plate with eccentric hole under tension.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_14 returns the stress concentration factor for a finite width plate with an eccentric hole subject to tension applied along its length.

Routines.Name: SCF_15
Routines.DisplayName: Plate with infinite row of holes under tension
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for plate with infinite row of holes under tension.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_15 returns the stress concentration factor for a finite width plate with an infinite inline row of holes along its length subject to tension.

Routines.Name: SCF_16
Routines.DisplayName: Circular Tube/Cylinder with transverse hole under tension
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the stress concentration factor for circular tube/cylinder with transverse hole under tension.
Routines.LongDescription: Function SCF_16 returns the stress concentration factor for either a hollow tube or solid cylinder with a transverse hole of diameter d_h subject to tension.

Routines.Name: Phi_TS
Routines.DisplayName: Thermal stress and deflection integral
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the Phi integral used to calculate thermal stress or axial deflection in rods with temperature gradients.
Routines.LongDescription: Function Phi_TS evaluates the integral of thermal expansion relative to an initial temperature, weighted by temperature-dependent thermal conductivity, for an incompressible substance. The result is used with integrated conductivity to calculate thermally induced stress or axial deflection in a rod with a temperature gradient.

Routines.Name: DebyeC
Routines.DisplayName: Debye-model specific heat
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the Debye-model ratio of specific heat capacity to the universal gas constant.
Routines.LongDescription: Function DebyeC evaluates the Debye model for a solid's specific heat. It returns the ratio of specific heat capacity to the universal gas constant as a function of absolute temperature divided by Debye temperature.

Routines.Name: DebyeU
Routines.DisplayName: Debye-model internal energy
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the Debye-model ratio of internal energy to the product of the universal gas constant and absolute temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: Function DebyeU evaluates the Debye model for a solid's internal energy. It returns the ratio of internal energy to the product of the universal gas constant and absolute temperature as a function of absolute temperature divided by Debye temperature.

Routines.Name: StdAtm_1976

Routines.Name: D_12_gas
Routines.DisplayName: Binary gas diffusion coefficient
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the binary diffusion coefficient for two gases.
Routines.LongDescription: Function D_12_gas calculates the binary diffusion coefficient for two gases using the Chapman-Enskog relation presented by Poling et al.

Routines.Name: D_12_liquid
Routines.DisplayName: Binary liquid diffusion coefficient
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the binary diffusion coefficient of a solute in a liquid solvent at infinite dilution.
Routines.LongDescription: Function D_12_liquid estimates the diffusion coefficient of species 1 in species 2 at infinite dilution using a modification of the Tyn and Calus method.

Routines.Name: D_11_gas
Routines.DisplayName: Gas self-diffusion coefficient
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns the self-diffusion coefficient for a pure gas.
Routines.LongDescription: Function D_11_gas calculates the self-diffusion coefficient for a pure gas in the EES database using the Ruckenstein and Liu method.

Routines.Name: P_2f

Routines.Name: VoltTC
Routines.DisplayName: Thermocouple voltage
Routines.ShortDescription: Returns thermocouple voltage for a supported thermocouple type at a specified temperature.
Routines.LongDescription: Function VoltTC evaluates the NIST ITS-90 polynomial curve fits to return thermocouple voltage in millivolts for thermocouple types E, B, J, K, N, R, and T at a specified temperature in degrees Celsius.
